x: Azrith's player was absent this session, so the GM ran Azrith. The GM's recap added a detail not recorded before: besides sending the party to Havenport to lie low, Duke Tristan Blackwood has instructed them to seek out Mauve Marigold and stay with her until he sends word. The spelling of her name is unconfirmed. The party turned down any last shopping or drinking. Cassian was glad to leave behind "these nobles marching around with their pretentious attitudes," and Odine called them "a bunch of fakers." After a long rest, they reported at dawn to the Blackwood camp. Captain Garan was waiting at attention with a few knights. He rebuffed Cassian's offer of a hug ("just personal space, man") and slung a massive bag of coin over his shoulder. The party would not be walking to Havenport: Blackwood had secured permission to use the teleportation circle in the Gleaming Keep. Source: Transcript. The party climbed the King's Road to the Gleaming Keep, its metal walls blazing in the sunrise. Oathkeepers at the open metal doors checked Garan's name against their list and let them in. It was the party's first time inside King Aldrich's castle. Cassian's Perception check (23) took in the interior. The walls had once been pristine stonework, perhaps by master masons, dwarves or elves, and King Aldrich's archmages had transmuted them to near-impenetrable steel. The halls held ornate pews, banners and candelabra, but the place was vast and hollow, kept only by "bannerless knights" guarding it from the noble houses. Cassian was left open-mouthed, and Odine walked straight into his back while gawking. In the circle chamber, six Oathkeeper knights and a robed acolyte greeted "party Blackwood." Garan dropped the bag on a table, spilling roughly 5,000 gp of Blackwood's money as tribute, and handed over a crystal vial of bluish-silver liquid. Source: Transcript. The acolyte named the liquid spell draught. It is a transmuted liquid made from the mana crystals mined in the Thornwood Vale, the crystals House Godrin harvests whenever it holds the Vale's deed. According to the acolyte, it took nearly 60 years to learn how to use it, and House Godrin was influential in its discovery. It is the only known way to power the circle, which connects to a few other key circles surviving from King Aldrich's time. He traced the circle's grooves with the draught, and they glowed and hummed. He then handed Aldrich a plate-sized metal keystone and told him to stand in the center and speak the destination's name. Aldrich was worried, after Cassian's jokes, that he might leave parts of himself behind. He raised the keystone and said "Havenport." Just before he did, Azrith started to ask "hey wait, before we go, shouldn't we—" and was cut off. It is not recorded whether Garan came with them. Source: Transcript. The party landed in a tarnished, neglected version of the Gleaming Keep's metal halls: Westermere Manor on the cliffs above Havenport. A lone Oathkeeper rose from his chair, surprised by visitors. He was Ian, a long-stationed knight with a white, unkempt beard. Cassian later called him "Ian Wren"; that surname is unconfirmed. Ian took back the keystone and recognized Cassian's name at once: "Lord Fortescue's son," adding that "people tend to have short memories." He also treated Havenport as Aldrich's home, asking how long it had been since he'd returned. Aldrich said about eight or nine years, perhaps longer. He admitted to "a little bit of a past there" but said he tends not to reminisce, even about the fall of House Westermere, the manor's former family. The town has been in disarray ever since. Source: Transcript. Ian laid out Havenport's troubles. There is a growing infestation of undead beneath the manor, and "Mav and her people" have taken refuge from it in the village. Ian keeps safe with an amulet that he says keeps the dead away, and he tries to warn off the village children who wander up at night. Meanwhile the Wither, which he named himself, has been taking more and more of the weak and sick in Havenport. Odine told him her own home is in the Vale. Asked where the blight comes from, Ian told the veteran Oathkeepers' legend of the Dark King (also called the Nightmare King). This was a ruler from a "far realm," not of men, elves or dwarves, and "the very essence of corruption itself." It began by using fairies and will-o'-wisps to lure children to their doom, then learned to corrupt people from within and make them part of its mind. King Aldrich marched against it with all his forces and nearly lost; Ian's own grandfather fought beside him. Then Aldrich withdrew his troops and went on alone with only his elite circle of mages. The Dark King was defeated, and "all that was found left of him in the Vale was a statue of himself." Source: Transcript. The story hit Odine hard. She clutched her pendant and remembered once finding that very statue, alone in the forest: a human king kneeling with his sword in the ground. "I've seen this statue that you speak of with my own eyes," she said, shaking, and told Ian the tale sounded very similar to her family's stories. Aldrich and Cassian both knew versions of the legend from childhood; it is told across the realms of men. Ian added that no one knows what King Aldrich did that day, but the symptoms of the Wither resemble what their ancestors suffered back then. There is little literature in Havenport to research it, "perhaps amongst the wealthy... but these people here are very much humble folk, survivors." Ian stands his post alone, and a fellow Oathkeeper relieves him every two weeks. He pointed the party toward the Salt House, a former shipyard warehouse that is now the survivors' community center. He said they would likely want coin for lodging "but they aren't bad people." He also told them the ghosts are in the undercroft below the manor. Source: Transcript. Outside, rain lashed a decaying seaport. The town had once held perhaps 1,000–5,000 people, with ragged ships at the docks and farmland behind, but now its only lights were in the Salt House. Rather than wait out the rain, the party went down into the undercroft, with Aldrich leading and Odine at the rear. The manor looked 10–15 years abandoned. In the first large room, an archway to a hallway was blocked by a floating sphere of swirling black mist. Cassian's Arcana check was a natural 1, and he pretended to taste it. Odine reached toward it with one hand on her pendant and spoke to it telepathically. It whispered back one word: "door." While Odine urged caution, Azrith took a running jump into the sphere, which shrank and vanished with him inside. "This isn't the first time he's just disappeared on us," Odine sighed. Source: Transcript. A silvery ghost drifted out of a room beyond: Samantha Westermere. "Bold of your friend to take the gate," she said. The sphere is the Curtain, "a curtain to the realm of death" and a passage between the ethereal and material planes. Azrith may come back "if he survives," when it reopens; that could be a day or a week, and the timing is unpredictable. Samantha said the manor belonged to her family, and she died in her own room down here after "many catastrophes" brought her house down. She refuses to pass on until the living restore Havenport to how it was in her childhood. Cassian flirted, and she blushed, as much as a ghost can. She offered them rooms but warned that residents of "the other side" might try to possess them. She led them to a black veil, a shimmering black wall sealing off part of the undercroft ever since the Curtain opened. It is impenetrable to her. She said much of the undercroft has "fallen into the ethereal realm." Source: Transcript. Odine's History check (14) told her this was not elven magic. It felt foreign and alien: the ethereal and material planes, normally separate, were converging here. Her Mage Hand did nothing against the veil. When she touched it with her own palm, it felt like cold steel, and black mist crawled up her arm, stealing her warmth. It didn't feel evil, but it felt like entropy. She channeled Sacred Flame through her palm, and the radiant light drove the shadow back. Cassian then tried it himself. Odine warned him telepathically ("be careful, it's really strong") as the shadow crept up his arm, "almost like it's turning your essence into living shadow." His magic check (a natural 20) found that no one is casting a spell there. The wall itself is the source, and whatever lies beyond it is reaching through. His Light cantrip showed that the wall swallows light completely. Samantha, who had learned "more in the last five minutes than in the last five years," said the wall wasn't there in her lifetime and is likely tied to the Curtain. She added that both the living and the dead use the Curtain, "some of them are vile," and that traffic has grown as more people have died in recent years. Source: Transcript. With night approaching and Azrith gone, the party decided to find lodging in town and come back later, possibly to pass through the Curtain together ("I've seen it done," Samantha said). Cassian promised Samantha they would return ("A Fortescue always keeps their promise"), and they walked out into the rain toward the Salt House. The session ended there. Source: Transcript. Azrith is lost through the Curtain into "the realm of death." He may return if he survives, whenever the Curtain reopens, which could be a day or a week. The party plans to come back and possibly go through together. His last, cut-off question ("shouldn't we—") is unanswered. Mauve Marigold: Blackwood's contact in Havenport. The party must stay with her until he sends word. Not yet found; she may be among the survivors at the Salt House (unconfirmed). The Salt House: the party is heading there for lodging, which will likely cost coin. The black veil: what lies beyond it, why radiant light repels it, and whether it is tied to the Curtain. Odine believes she can figure it out. The Dark King legend: what King Aldrich did, the kneeling statue Odine has seen in the Vale, and the parallels to her family's stories and the Wither. See Investigate the Pestilence. Havenport's decline: the fall of House Westermere, the undead beneath the manor, the Wither's toll, and village children wandering near the undercroft. Aldrich's past in Havenport: he confirmed this is his home, but is reluctant to talk about it. Samantha Westermere: refuses to pass on until Havenport is restored. She warned about possession, and Cassian promised to return. Spell draught: its link to House Godrin's Vale mana crystals and to the teleportation network makes the Vale deed matter even more. Whether Captain Garan teleported with the party or stayed in Everdale is not recorded. Picking up mid-scene in the Menagerie, Aldrich capped off the party's chaotic manticore bout by casting Firebolt into the arena's outer tents and banners as a parting smokescreen, and the party fled through the tunnel amid the judges' confusion. At the contenders' tent, Holt was aghast—calling it "the most disrespectful performance" he'd seen in the games and warning that the game makers and noble houses would be furious enough to end the party's tournament run outright, urging them to leave quickly before anyone could react. Source: Transcript. At the Ragged Flagon, Rory revealed he'd bet against the party and won, but still poured free drinks (two per head, with Aldrich's new brass King's Cup mug filled specially) and warned them to watch their backs—"those nobles, they like to play dirty." Two patrons, a half-orc and a dwarf, praised the spectacle as legendary, singling out the burning banners; the dwarf—revealed to be kin to "Old Ironhide," the dwarf who died in the King's Cup—declared the party was becoming folk heroes among the common crowd, even as the nobility fumed. Source: Transcript. Mid-celebration, Renny Blackwood arrived breathless with an urgent summons from Duke Tristan Blackwood. En route, the party met two new figures: Captain Garan, Blackwood's stern captain of the guard, who cryptically warned "you wagered and lost, but the duke is wagering his name" and told them to be careful "what you've set off"; and Lady Elwyn Blackwood, the duke's wife, who brushed off Garan's tension and told them she found the change of pace refreshing. Odine's Insight check (13) read her as a sharp social operator, distinct from her husband's more strategic style. Source: Transcript. Alone with the party, Duke Blackwood's stern silence broke into open delight: "That was fucking genius." He admonished them for spending so much of his money but admitted their outcome—"the creature lives, my people live"—served him better than anything he could have planned: the scandal makes the party a perfect distraction, drawing every noble eye away from his other dealings. He warned soberly that mercy will eventually cost lives, and that he expects the party to own the consequences whenever their judgment overrides orders like his. Unable to reward them financially while he recoups his gambling losses, he instead arranged for Captain Garan to escort the party out of the fairgrounds to a town called Havenport to let tensions cool. As they left, Aldrich reacted oddly to the name—it's his own surname, one he's only ever known from family bedtime stories—prompting a private, undisclosed aside between the GM and Aldrich's player. Source: Transcript. Back at camp, Odine—newly wary of the camp's unfamiliar faces after the day's events—suggested the party start keeping watches or find more secure lodging. Before turning in, Odine reached out to Jevon via her sending stone to let him know where the party was heading; the party recalled that Jevon had since left Everdale for an outpost on the western fringe of the Thornwood Vale, hoping to help distract or mislead the House Godrin scouting party now chasing Odine's decoy lead. Odine kept first watch herself (Perception 19, a safe night), taking on an extra point of exhaustion for it. The session closed with the whole party reaching level 5—a narrative milestone rather than a loot reward—with Azrith and Aldrich both gaining Extra Attack, and Odine advancing to Sorcerer 3 / Warlock 2. Source: Transcript. Aldrich's surname and Havenport: Duke Blackwood is sending the party to a town called Havenport—the same name as Aldrich's own surname, which he only knows from family bedtime stories. A private GM/player aside was held off-page; the connection is unresolved and likely significant to Aldrich's backstory. Duke Blackwood's warning: "there will come a day when mercy costs lives"—an implicit test of the party's judgment going forward. Camp security: Odine's suggestion to start night watches or relocate to safer lodging was raised but not yet acted on. House Godrin's scouting party is actively chasing Odine's decoy lead toward the western Thornwood Vale, where Jevon has gone to help misdirect them—outcome unresolved. The freed manticore's whereabouts: idly speculated on by the party (mountains?) but unknown; Cassian believes it will find them again if it wants to. Political fallout from the Menagerie stunt: Captain Garan's warning that the party doesn't know "what they've set off" remains unexplained. The session opened directly into the Menagerie bout against the manticore, with Aldrich and Odine Dunmere still carrying exhaustion level 1 (a flat −2 on all d20 tests and −5 ft speed under the 2024 rules). The manticore struck first from the air with a ranged tail-spike attack, wounding Cassian. Cassian opened by casting Sleep on it mid-flight (DC 14 Wisdom save, failed)—it dropped unconscious, crashed to the ground for 10 bludgeoning damage, and woke up prone from the fall. Azrith and Odine both landed early hits (a dagger strike and a cold Sorcerous Burst), while Aldrich's Firebolt went wide. Source: Transcript. As the fight wore on, the manticore began speaking in Common—clearly a magically or arcanely bound creature, not a mindless beast—taunting the party ("Soft little heroes playing at glory. Which shall I devour first?"). Cassian saw an opening and pivoted to persuasion instead of violence: offering it food, freedom, and a place with the party rather than death. A 23 landed part of the pitch—the manticore visibly weighs the offer against a deep fear of "its masters," and drops to two attacks a round instead of three. Azrith and Odine, not yet aware of the shift, kept fighting (Chill Touch hits, a quickened Mind Sliver plus Thunderwave from Odine); the manticore, feeling doubly betrayed by mixed signals, snarled "DECEIVERS! Never trust mortals!" and turned its full fury on Azrith, landing two of three rend attacks for 21 combined damage. Aldrich, catching on to Cassian's plan, physically shoved Azrith out of the fight with a natural-20 Athletics check to stop him from attacking further. Source: Transcript. Cassian pressed the case a final time—refusing to trade blow for blow, offering to help the manticore escape instead—and rolled a 25 Persuasion. The manticore broke: it revealed that its true captors would kill it regardless of the fight's outcome, and pointed out a trebuchet rigged with a steel net positioned to recapture anything that tried to flee the arena—its actual leash. Cassian mounted the manticore, flew it to the trebuchet crew, and cast Charm Person on the operator (DC 13, failed save) to stand him down; the manticore then tore the trebuchet apart. Freed, it asked Cassian's name, thanked him for making it "a free manticore," and set off to find a name of its own, promising to visit the party's camp for meat and ale. Source: Transcript. While this played out, Odine and Aldrich worked the crowd rather than the fight: Odine cast Cause Fear on the loudest heckler to seed a mild crowd panic (failed save), openly condemning the spectacle as "cold-blooded murder, not a test"—drawing a "She's a witch!" shout from the stands. Aldrich used Thaumaturgy's phantom sound and booming voice to whisper unsettling phrases into the judges' box, sowing further confusion among officials. The arena's crowd-approval checks, run each round, failed twice and were abandoned by round 5 as "too far gone"—the party was visibly losing the crowd even as they won the moral outcome. From the air, Cassian spotted a cliffside above the stadium crowded with peasants who couldn't afford Menagerie seats; as he flew off with the freed manticore, they cheered the party as heroes, in stark contrast to the booing paying crowd below. Source: Transcript. The session closed with Cassian delivering a booming speech to the arena—framing the outcome as proof "not every creature brought in here is willing to die or to stay owned," and inviting anyone who "knows the weight of another man's chains" to cheer instead of jeer—backed by Odine's illusory bowing manticore (Silent Image) and Aldrich handing Azrith a healing potion. A follow-up Persuasion check (22, even after Heroic Inspiration) won over only part of the crowd: officials were furious and openly unsure how to score the bout (one threw his clipboard), and Duke Tristan Blackwood—the party's sponsor—was seen trying to slip out of the noble box without meeting anyone's eyes. The GM confirmed the party has drawn more attention than a clean kill would have—for better or worse—and ended the session to consider the fallout. Source: Transcript. The freed manticore: unnamed as of departure, promised to visit the party's camp. A potential ally, currently unnamed and unlocated. Duke Tristan Blackwood's reaction: he avoided eye contact and tried to leave quietly—the party's sponsor may be embarrassed or endangered by their unconventional stunt. Not yet addressed on-page. The judges/officials: furious and unable to agree on how to score the bout. Consequences for the party's standing in the tournament are unresolved. Crowd reputation split: the paying Menagerie crowd largely turned against the party (booing, "she's a witch"), while the peasant onlookers on the cliffside now see them as heroes. Long-term reputation effects unclear. Odine's public display of Cause Fear and the "witch" accusation shouted from the crowd—unresolved social fallout. Picking up immediately after the King's Cup, the party carried an exhaustion-level-6 Aldrich toward the King's Fair healer tents, with Azrith (returned from his unexplained overnight absence) helping. A history check pointed them toward clerics from House Oswall, but the party found a friendlier option first: Father Kaldus Vey, a priest of the Royal Chapel working the healer tents. For 100 gp of diamond dust plus a 300 gp materials fee and a 100 gp donation (400 gp total), he agreed to spend the evening casting Greater Restoration on Aldrich, capped at three castings per day. Overnight care plus a long rest cleared Aldrich from exhaustion 6 down to 1; Odine Dunmere cleared her own King's Cup exhaustion down to 1 as well. Source: Transcript. While Aldrich recovered, Cassian and Azrith slipped out to finally infiltrate White Feather Tor, the House Godrin camp, using the intelligence map Duke Tristan Blackwood had provided. Both went in invisible—Cassian via a warlock spell (upcast to cover Azrith too), sustaining it while flying above the camp using his Celestial Revelation wings; Azrith on foot, shimmying up between two close-set gate pillars after a failed first attempt, then landing a quiet stealth check to slip inside undetected. Two patrolling knights nearly spotted Cassian and Azrith in the treeline beforehand but wrote it off as nothing. Source: Transcript. Inside, Azrith reached the Messenger Tent and found it empty but locked down tight—crates and drawers secured with padlocks. He lifted a guard's keyring with a Sleight of Hand check (rerolled via Heroic Inspiration to a 23), used it to open a table drawer, and recovered an already-opened letter bearing House Godrin's broken seal. A separate strongbox yielded 73 gp and a potion of healing, which he took satchel and all. Cassian, unable to get anything useful from the empty Messenger Tent, instead eavesdropped on the camp's main tent and made out a fragment of a hushed conversation he identified (History check) as Percival Godrin's voice: "Keep your voice down. They're not chasing a ghost. She's alive. We've already confirmed it." Circling the camp once more before leaving, Cassian spotted House Godrin's champion for the first time: a nearly 9–10-foot-tall knight in arcane relic armor and helm, wielding an enchanted axe, known at the tournaments as "the Crow"—Sir Thorin Cassavar. Cassian and Azrith regrouped in the woods, compared notes, and returned to camp to find Odine already asleep. Source: Transcript. The letter Azrith recovered confirmed what Cassian overheard: House Godrin believes Maralynn—the witch the party has only known as Jevon's teacher—is alive and has been located, not the "ghost" or dead legend they'd been treating her as. The next morning, with Aldrich still recovering (napping through the day at Father Kaldus Vey's suggestion to shed one more exhaustion level, and getting good-natured ribbing from the priest about his "blood curse" tiefling heritage), Cassian, Odine, and Azrith brought the letter directly to Duke Tristan Blackwood at Clover Hill via Renny Blackwood's emergency access. Blackwood only knew the name from folklore—an archmage called Marlin who once served King Aldric the Wise, presumed dead since "the ancient war"—but Odine, hedging carefully, confirmed there may really be a Marlin alive in the Vale. Reading the Godrin letter rattled Blackwood: he concluded he has a mole feeding House Godrin information about his own dealings (he admitted to having "flirted with one of their nieces"), and that Godrin already knows he is sponsoring the party. Source: Transcript. To buy time and protect the real Maralynn, Odine improvised a decoy: a fabricated name, Erendel Morath, and a location deep in the Thornwood Vale far from home, framed as a dangerous, self-sufficient "witch" who could hold her own against Godrin agents for days. She backed the lie with a genuine token—the charm pendant from her home village, removed from her necklace and handed to Blackwood—to make the false lead convincing enough to feed through his own intelligence channels as a diversion. Blackwood agreed to float it. Separately, Cassian checked in with Jevon (off-page, via message), telling him House Godrin's real target is his old teacher, not him—Jevon confirmed Maralynn is the one who trained him and hasn't seen her in years, and is now weighing whether to search for her himself rather than wait. Source: Transcript. Back at camp, the party finalized their gear ahead of that evening's Menagerie bout—Aldrich's commissioned splint armor, Azrith's half-paid +1 scimitar, Cassian studying his Eyes of Charming, Odine confirming her attunement to the Shadowfell Shard—and reported to Holt's team at the arena. Renny Blackwood left them a short note wishing them luck ("shorthanded on such short notice... don't die"). Cassian's Unseen Servant, sent ahead to scout the prior match in their bracket, reported four black knights fighting a beast that let out a deep, lion-like roar; its own rudimentary sketch confirmed a manticore. Walking out to a roaring crowd and an unfazed manticore, Odine attempted an opening Intimidation check (14, using Heroic Inspiration) that failed to faze the beast. The session ended there, with combat and initiative to be rolled at the start of the next session. Source: Transcript. The Menagerie bout vs. a manticore: about to begin: initiative not yet rolled. Aldrich and Odine both enter at exhaustion level 1. Sir Thorin Cassavar ("the Crow"): House Godrin's champion, seen for the first time at White Feather Tor—not yet engaged, but a serious combat threat if the party crosses paths with him directly. Maralynn confirmed alive: House Godrin has located her, per the intercepted letter and overheard conversation. Jevon is weighing whether to search for her himself. The decoy plan: Odine's false lead (Erendel Morath) is now in Duke Blackwood's hands to float through his channels—outcome unresolved. Blackwood's mole: he suspects a leak in his own camp (possibly tied to a Godrin niece he "flirted with")—not identified or resolved. The stolen satchel's contents: 73 gp, a potion of healing, and an unread second letter ("people who travel without banners") Azrith only skimmed—not yet followed up on. Azrith was absent this session—handled in-fiction the same way as his prior disappearance: he slipped out in the night on unstated business ("probably sniffing rocks or picking flowers," per Cassian), expected back before the next bout. He did not appear on-page. With a day and a half before the party's Menagerie bout, Odine Dunmere pushed to investigate House Godrin directly to learn why they want Jevon. The party first went to finally take up Duke Tristan Blackwood's invitation at Clover Hill. His attendant led them past two guards to the Duke, boots up on his desk, smoking an emberleaf cigar. After dismissing his guards for privacy, Blackwood asked each PC's origin: Aldrich confirmed he once served House Troth, a minor vassal house of House Wulfhelm, before leaving "the seaside" to see the world; Cassian confirmed House Fortescue has been a Wulfhelm vassal for roughly 60 years—which visibly surprised Blackwood, who said he's never once heard Wulfhelm acknowledge Fortescue as a vassal despite "running in a lot of circles," a discrepancy Cassian deflected ("there are few who remember us fondly"); and Odine haltingly explained she is "from beyond the Vale" (evasively; she denied to Blackwood that her homeland was in the Vale), seeking a way to save her homeland from a crop-killing blight. Blackwood supplied the word himself—"a blight, yes?"—and confirmed the blight has begun spreading into the Crownlands themselves, not just the Thornwood Vale. Source: Transcript. Blackwood then laid out the tournament's real political stakes. House Godrin and House Wulfhelm have traded control of the Thornwood Vale between them for nearly a decade via the King's Tourney (Wulfhelm currently holds the deed, from last year's win); House Corwyn believes the Vale conceals a secret that could unite the lesser houses against Godrin and Wulfhelm, and has sought it for nearly a century but cannot act without holding the Vale's title. Per Blackwood: "Godrin believes this year's tournament already belongs to them. Wolfhelm believes their strength and status entitles them to it. Corwyn believes they are clever enough to understand everyone else's game." He personally would relish seeing all three great houses lose this year—unprecedented in a century of the tournament. He warned the party that House Godrin has been unusually active lately, "asking a lot of questions" and "sticking their noses in shady corners"—there are rumors they've been kidnapping children. Blackwood revealed that as a young competitor himself, he once personally discovered House Godrin abducting hedge mages, and wonders what "frightened one of the most powerful arcane families in the Crownlands badly enough to resort to kidnapping." He framed the party's edge plainly: "Nobody owns you... I wouldn't claim to own you, of course. Never confuse the two." He handed Cassian a sealed intelligence note—names and locations tied to House Godrin's camp activity—and advised investigating at night. He gave Cassian a second emberleaf cigar as a parting gift. Source: Transcript. At the Ragged Flagon, Rory confirmed the party's Menagerie opponent: Kardis Wulfhelm, prince and heir of House Wulfhelm, one of the best (if not the best) swordsmen in his house. At Holt's registration board this was confirmed publicly, along with word that both camps have been unusually busy scouting each other. Reviewing Blackwood's note together, Aldrich (playing at illiteracy) pointed blindly at the page and landed—apparently by accident—on its key location: the Messenger Tent at White Feather Tor. The party scouted the tor from a distance: the front gate is heavily guarded (4–5 knights, high walls—the worst approach), but Odine's Perception check (natural 20) found a sheer cliffside on another face of the hill that could be climbed at night to get in unseen. The infiltration itself was deferred; the party returned to the Ragged Flagon first for the evening's entertainment. Source: Transcript. That entertainment was the King's Cup, Rory's weekly drinking tournament: escalating DC Constitution saves against 18 other contestants, two consecutive failures (or one natural 1) costing a level of exhaustion. Cassian sponsored Odine and Aldrich into the field. Odine held her own for two rounds, rigged a side bet against her own success (Deception 14), then failed out at exhaustion level 2, vomiting and bowing out. Aldrich did not stop. He fought through repeated exhaustion, burned his Heroic Inspiration reroll to survive the frost-giant liqueur round, and came down to a final head-to-head against an unnamed dwarf. On the last, unnamed mystery shot—"King's Mistake"—both drinkers failed their save. The dwarf died on the spot ("meeting his ancestors... a hero's death," refusing to concede for his clan's name). Aldrich survived but was driven to exhaustion level 6, functionally incapacitated. He was declared champion of the King's Cup: 90 gold pieces and an oversized ornate brass drinking mug. Cassian scanned the noble box (22 perception) and caught the eye of Duke Tristan Blackwood, a midlord of House Blackwood—a vassal house, not one of the big three—who had walked to the table with his goblet during the fight. He gave Cassian a golf-clap nod; Cassian winked back. Source: Transcript. Speaking to the game master after the bout, the party learned one more successful showing would bring them to Level 5 crowd favor and grant entry into the big leagues. Three options for the next contest were offered: a team bout against another group of four, skill challenges (obstacle-type), or a gauntlet (wave battle against monsters/beasts). The party opted to rest at least a day first. Cassian then checked the 5-gold wager slip—the terms required that no ally be knocked unconscious. Both Cassian and Azrith had gone down. The bet is technically lost. Cassian plans to argue to the coin master that the party "walked out on their feet." The session ended with the party preparing for recovery, potential sponsorship from Duke Blackwood, and the next tournament decision ahead. Source: Transcript. The party arrived at the Ragged Flagon, the makeshift campground tavern Jevon had recommended as a safe place to lie low. Inside they found Rory, an orc bartender running a cheap but busy establishment catering to common folk and tournament participants. Aldrich bought a round of house ale (one silver each), and Cassian introduced the group to Rory. As Azrith quietly circled the room, a natural 20 on perception revealed Gruvelda Duskbelt sitting in a corner booth—heavily cloaked, keeping a low profile, already on her second goblet. The entire party immediately crowded her table, drawing a withering look and a fat dwarven finger pressed to her lips: sit down, be quiet. The group made their case. Aldrich lowered his collar to show the residual necrosis from the life drain attack in the Stone Sanctum graveyard as physical proof. A moderate persuasion check (12) got Gruvelda halfway. Cassian then quietly revealed his family signet ring—shaped like a falling star that meets its tail, ouroboros-like—marking him as a member of an old noble house, a vassal line under House Wulfhelm. Gruvelda, who respects old bloodlines over the ambitious new houses crowding the tournament, was moved: "Have always found success betting on the dark horse. Fine. You've earned a shield for your first bout. If you succeed and I'll be watching, then I'll armor one of you." She also asked them to keep quiet about seeing her there and returned to her ale. Source: Transcript. With lodging needed for the night, Cassian led the party to Boarhead Tor, the elevated section of the noble camp hill where great houses had erected elegant silk tents, stabled prize horses, and posted guards in white and gold. The bedchamber Cassian targeted had been reserved by Kardis Wulfhelm for his return party later that night. The noble servant guarding it would not budge. Cassian talked the servant into lending his own personal tent for the night instead (persuasion 18). The party squeezed in for a long rest. Odine Dunmere cast Firebolt at the brazier to heat the tent before collapsing onto a bedroll. Source: Transcript. During the long rest, Cassian had a dream. He found himself back at the Ragged Flagon when a masked figure approached—the same entity that had appeared in a prior dream and gifted him his dice. The figure wore trimmed gown and regalia and a mask concealing nearly the entire face, with only mischievous eyes visible. It called Cassian "clever boy" and opened negotiations. They struck a wager: Cassian would continue stirring trouble among the noble houses and keep the party together—with specific emphasis on keeping Odine close ("I find her interesting and relevant; don't let her out of your sight"). In exchange, the entity would pull strings to remove "immovable roadblocks"—naming Ser Calder Ross, House Wulfhelm's prized champion, and House Godrin's champion as the principal threats. Cassian's counter-demand: find out how his family came to possess the dice. The entity agreed to deliver that answer before the final bout. Cassian covered for the dream when Azrith (who had not slept) asked, claiming he had dreamed about a woman. Source: Transcript. At dawn, the party returned to Gruvelda Duskbelt's tent in the King's Tourney grounds. Gruvelda presented Aldrich with a Sentinel Shield: blue-painted dwarven craftsmanship bearing an eye emblem. The shield grants advantage on both initiative rolls and perception checks, but requires an action to equip or stow (trading offense for defense mid-fight). She then rewarded each party member with 4 gold coins and pointed them toward a future lead: "If you ever find your way to the Vale, look up my brother Grimhall Duskbelt. If you're truly ghost hunters, he may have use for you and more coin." Grimhall is a dwarven lord in the Thornwood Vale, contending with shadows and ghouls he believes originate in this town rather than in the Vale. Source: Transcript. Before their own bout, the party watched several groups compete in the Proving Grounds. The format is multi-phase—part puzzle-solving, part survival against dangerous beasts. A bear was released on one group. One standout party of young farm boys from several villages worked in tight formation and overwhelmed every challenge with raw coordinated strength; they were immediately surrounded by scouts and potential sponsors afterward. Other parties fared far worse—incapacitated, limping out, or simply embarrassed in the mud. Cassian, eyeing the betting rings, approached a bookmaker and wagered 5 gold (4 of his own plus 1 from Aldrich) that the party would win their bout without anyone being incapacitated, posing as an outside bettor. If the party wins clean, they collect 10 gold. Source: Transcript. As the Proving Grounds took a midday recess, Virellan Le'Strange emerged from the crowd and offered the party a flamboyant word of encouragement before their evening slot. The session ended with the party preparing to report to Tent D for their first bout at sundown. Source: Transcript. The session picked up at the King's Tourney with the party regrouped after learning Jevon was taken by white-armored knights. Cassian led Aldrich and the others to the tent of Gruvelda Duskbelt, one of the few dwarves at the fair and a master smith. Aldrich hoped to buy armor or weapons, but with only 44 gold total the best Gruvelda could offer was a round shield, and she laughed off Cassian's attempts to charm her. Azrith broke the standoff by using Thaumaturgy to conjure phantom ghostly sounds around her tent, pitching the party as ghost hunters who could solve a problem she'd heard about. Intrigued, Gruvelda pulled the group inside and told them her clan had heard rumors that certain nobles were meddling with magic at the hamlet cemetery on the hill. She offered to craft something for Aldrich before the tournament and put word in with her brother—who guards her clan's home in the Vale from shadows and ghouls—if the party dealt with the ghosts and brought her proof. As the group prepared to leave, Gruvelda stopped Odine Dunmere and asked why she had come from the Vale. When Odine mentioned the pestilence, Gruvelda retrieved a small wooden box from her shelf, opened it, and revealed a severed, heavily decayed hand covered in the same black vine-like veins as the curse. She then removed a glove from her other hand to show a prosthetic nub: she had cut off her own hand years ago to stop the corruption from consuming her. Odine, overwhelmed by shock, uncontrollably cast Message into Gruvelda's mind before she realized she was doing it. She then drew back her sleeve to reveal the tentacle-like marks on her own arm. Gruvelda said flatly that none of the people at the fair knew what was coming. She agreed to speak with Odine in depth but asked her to wait until the first week of the festival was over, as she would be too busy until then. Source: Transcript. The party climbed from the King's Tourney grounds up into the hamlet of Everdale proper, a sleepy hilltop village quiet compared to the fairgrounds. Oathkeeper patrols walked the streets in pairs, bearing three distinct banners: a green shield with a stag (the same order as the knight Sir Televast, encountered before reaching the city), a red shield with an ember flame, and a silver crest with a helm and two crossed swords. Cassian noted these are the three oldest surviving knightly orders from the era of King Aldrich—the orders that formed the Oathkeepers and have kept the throne and keep safe ever since. From the crest of the hill, Odine could see the Thornwood Vale stretching beyond the Gleaming Keep—a vast forested valley veiled in an almost imperceptible green mist. Azrith's supernatural senses guided the party to the Stone Sanctum, an old moss-and-vine-covered stone cathedral with a bell tower and an attached graveyard. Inside the dim chapel, Cassian played with Thaumaturgy to lighten the mood; the resulting disturbance dislodged a scrap of green fabric from an iron candelabra that Azrith identified as likely torn from Jevon's cloak. When Odine opened Jevon's magical box, its light flickered erratically instead of glowing steadily—a sign to her that his life force was in danger. She bolted into the graveyard and found Jevon bound in rope and tied to a cherubim statue, unconscious and bloodied. A dead black knight lay on the ground nearby. Odine cast Healing Word and brought Jevon back to consciousness. He immediately warned that there had been a second knight. Before the party could react, the second black knight—possessed by an undead spirit—lunged from the shadows and grabbed Azrith, who flipped free (acrobatics, 19 vs. 18). Combat followed. Odine spent her first turn sawing through Jevon's ropes and freeing him. Aldrich struck the creature with an unarmed blow but failed to trip it and then absorbed its life drain attack: 4 necrotic damage that also permanently reduced his maximum hit points by 4 until a long rest. Azrith activated his Crimson Rite (Rite of Dawn), taking 1d4 necrotic damage to his hand in exchange for resistance to necrotic damage, a bright light aura, and bonus radiant damage against undead. Cassian misty stepped to Jevon's side and returned his box to him, then fired an Eldritch Blast (5 force damage). Jevon joined the fight with his Green-Flame Blade but missed. Odine blasted the creature with Sorcerous Burst, dealing 13 lightning damage (halved to 6 against its resistance). The creature critically struck Azrith on its next turn, draining his max HP down to 12. Finally Azrith hit with his scimitar—his Rite making the attack magical and adding radiant dice—finishing the creature. As the armored body dropped, a spectral form emerged, said "I submit, I must go," and dissipated. The party searched the knight's distorted body and Cassian identified the crest: these were House Godrin soldiers, likely common foot enforcers rather than decorated knights. Jevon, now on his feet, explained that the Godrin men had taken him to interrogate him about his magic and his teacher. His teacher is a witch named Maralynn, who found him near death, malnourished and near starving, and taught him to survive before moving on. She gave him his box and had been encountered in Everdale, but she is from the Thornwood Vale and wields what Jevon described as unfathomable power. Cassian speculated aloud that Maralynn may be what the noble houses are truly searching for when they compete over the deed to the Vale, and that House Godrin may be pressing Jevon to find her. Jevon said he could not safely return to the fair in daylight—when the Godrins discover their men are missing, suspicion will fall on him. He enchanted two small stones using his box: one for himself, one handed to Odine. She can use the stone to send him one brief message, and he can reply to her mind. He asked her to use it at night, once the party has a safe meeting place. For lodging, Jevon recommended the Ragged Flagon, a makeshift tavern in the King's Tourney campgrounds that noble houses tend to avoid, as a good place to lie low. He then slipped into the shadows to hide out for the coming days. The party's first bout in the Proving Grounds is the following evening at sundown. Source: Transcript. The party broke camp and continued toward Everdale for the King's Tourney. Odine Dunmere was shaken by the corrupted horse from the previous day because she has seen the same pestilence in the Thornwood Vale, where it affects animals, plants, and people. The horse suggested to her that the entity's malignant curse is spreading beyond the Vale. While speaking with Cassian, her sleeve slipped enough for him to notice black tentacle-like lines on her arm, similar to the corruption on the horse. He also noticed that her violet pendant is important to her, but he did not press her about it. As the road climbed toward Everdale, the party saw the city, the Gleaming Keep, and the massive festival grounds below it. Cassian explained what he knew of the city: the Empty Throne has remained unclaimed since King Aldrich, and the Oathkeepers guard the keep, throne, city, and tournament while the noble houses compete for status and influence. The King's Tourney is the city's great yearly event and the economic heart of the surrounding settlement. Jevon guided the party into the King's Tourney, then left them to enjoy themselves. Virellan Le'Strange, a flamboyant bard and observer, greeted the group and introduced Aldrich to Minnie, who sold him a bottle of huckleberry mead made from berries harvested near the Thornwood Vale. The party reached the registration tent, where Cassian recognized the white armor and banner of House Godrin, a wealthy and magically powerful noble house associated with mana crystals, artifacts, and ruthless ambition. Holt, the registrar, signed the party into the Proving Grounds for a 25 gold group fee. They registered under the name Cassian's Crushing Crusaders and were told to report to Tent D on the following in-game day at 6 PM. After registration, Cassian led the group to Slug's cookhouse. Odine was horrified by the open preparation of meat, but Slug found food she could tolerate and served the others smoked pork and mead. While eating, the party noticed Kardis Wulfhelm, prince of House Wulfhelm, enter with a black-armored companion. Aldrich recognized House Wulfhelm as the parent house of the vassal house he once served. Cassian knew the Wulfhelms won last year's tournament and currently hold the title and deed to the Thornwood Vale. The group then visited Marea Voss, an apothecary. Cassian haggled her into selling four healing potions for 38 gold total, split between him and Odine. Aldrich bought a Traveler's Tonic. When Odine mentioned the pestilence ravaging her home, Marea warned her to seek true sources and be wary of people exploiting misinformation about the pestilence. Outside, Azrith found Jevon's magical box buried in muddy cart tracks. A small boy said Jevon dropped it when white-armored knights took him. Away from Jevon, the box still glowed, but much more dimly. The party withdrew from the crowd to discuss what to do. Cassian warned that interfering with guards or noble soldiers could be dangerous, but Odine insisted they needed to help Jevon. The session ended with the group planning to split up for short errands, then meet again at sundown. Odine intended to study the box and see whether it could help locate Jevon, while Aldrich wanted to find a smithy. Boarhead Tor is the elevated noble camp hill at the King's Tourney grounds in Everdale. The great houses erect their finest silk tents here, stable prize horses, and post guards in house colors. It is cleaner and better-smelling than the common campgrounds, with music and revelry continuing even late at night. Source: 2026.05.19. House Wulfhelm maintains a significant presence here, marked by white and gold armor on their guards and banners posted throughout their section. Kardis Wulfhelm reserved a full bedchamber tent for his return party the night of the party's first visit. Cassian fast-talked a noble servant into lending his personal tent for one night by playing up his vassal house connection to House Wulfhelm. The servant made clear it was a one-time offer and that the party was not welcome back after the tournament. Access normally requires established house credentials; the servant warned that without them, the only alternatives are the common campgrounds or "Beggar's Rook" (a step further down that even Cassian dismissed as an insult). King's Tourney: Located within the tournament campgrounds. House Wulfhelm: Primary noble house with visible presence on the hill. Kardis Wulfhelm: Has reserved quarters here.

Clover Hill is the noble encampment area above the King's Tourney fairgrounds where higher-status houses and their vassals station their servants, tents, and supplies during the festival. Source: 2026.06.11. The party collected their sponsorship items from House Blackwood's servants here after Duke Tristan Blackwood finalized the sponsorship deal. Items delivered at Clover Hill: Combat Greaves (Aldrich), Cloak of Protection (Cassian), Ring of Scorching Ray (Odine Dunmere), and a Potion of Fire Breathing (party inventory). House Blackwood: Had servants and a supply tent stationed here during the tournament. King's Tourney: Adjacent noble encampment area. Boarhead Tor: Another elevated noble camp area at the tournament; Boarhead Tor is specifically associated with House Wulfhelm.

The Crown Gauntlet is an obstacle-course tournament format at the Proving Grounds: a roughly 40-foot wooden tower rising out of a mud pit, which all four members of a team must climb and reach together to ring a bell at the top. Cassian's Crushing Crusaders are the first team to complete it in over seven years. Source: 2026.06.23, 2026.07.14. Three negatively-sloped mud "steps," requiring a running start (Athletics/Acrobatics or slide back down). Three free-spinning balance logs on spindles, 10 ft off the ground. A sheer plank wall, climbable via thin cracks between the planks (base DC 18). A central tower with gear-driven rotating platforms, each turning 180° per 6-second round in alternating directions. A final guarded platform and the bell at the summit. Four obstacle guards are stationed along the course (two at the base, one at the wall platform, one at the top with a jousting baton); rules of engagement forbid lethal force against them—bludgeoning/incapacitation only. Performance is tracked by two meters: Cheer Marks (crowd-pleasing successes, tracked via d4 rolls) and Mud Marks (embarrassing failures). Filling Cheer Marks to 10/10 grants a team-wide boon; 10 Mud Marks triggers a team-wide bane. A countdown timer represents the time limit—running it out means being thrown in the mud pit and pelted with rotten produce by the crowd. Started 2026.06.23, paused mid-challenge at countdown 8 (Cheer Marks 7/10, Mud Marks 1/10) with three of four guards neutralized via Odine Dunmere's Hideous Laughter, Cassian's Phantasmal Force, and Odine's illusory owlbear (Silent Image). Concluded 2026.07.14: the party maxed Cheer Marks to 10/10 via Cassian's Thaumaturgy performance, cleared the wall (DC dropped to 15 by Azrith's natural-20 Investigation coaching), freed a jammed gear mechanism, and rang the bell together with six seconds left on the clock. Duke Tristan Blackwood watched from the sponsor's box with only a reserved slow clap. See Compete in the King's Tourney for the full wager and reward details. King's Tourney: The Gauntlet is a Proving Grounds format. Compete in the King's Tourney Duke Tristan Blackwood: Sponsor who watched the completion and later delivered the victory reward. Rory: Bet 25 gp against the party completing it, and lost.

The Empty Throne is the throne once held by King Aldrich in Everdale. It has remained unfilled for centuries while noble houses continue to war and compete for power. Source: 2026.05.05. Gleaming Keep Oathkeepers King's Tourney

Everdale is the human capital city and the host of the annual King's Tourney. Roads converge here toward a hill crowned by the Gleaming Keep, with the tournament grounds and King's Tourney spreading through the valley below. Source: 2026.05.05. Gleaming Keep: a keep built from stone supposedly transmuted into metal by King Aldrich's mages. It sits on a cliff above the city and reflects the light, giving it its name. Source: 2026.05.05. Empty Throne: the throne once held by King Aldrich. It has not been filled for centuries. Source: 2026.05.05. King's Tourney: a two-week annual tournament that brings Everdale to life and sustains much of the local economy. Source: 2026.05.05. Stone Sanctum: an old moss-and-vine-covered cathedral in the hamlet above the tourney grounds, with an attached graveyard. Source: 2026.05.12. Ragged Flagon: a makeshift tavern in the King's Tourney campgrounds where nobles don't typically frequent. Source: 2026.05.12. Boarhead Tor: the elevated noble camp hill where House Wulfhelm is based. Source: 2026.05.19. Clover Hill: the noble encampment above the fairgrounds, where Duke Tristan Blackwood keeps his tent. Source: 2026.06.11. Crown Gauntlet: the Proving Grounds' 40-foot obstacle tower, which the party cleared on 2026.07.14. The Menagerie: the beast-arena tier of the tourney, where the party freed a captive manticore. Source: 2026.08.11, 2026.09.08. White Feather Tor: House Godrin's family camp in the Eastern Tourney Grounds, which the party infiltrated on 2026.08.25. Everdale is protected and administered by the Oathkeepers, an order formed from three knightly orders. They protect the keep, guard the Empty Throne, police the tournament, and help oversee the local economy and settlement. They believe King Aldrich will someday return. Source: 2026.05.05. House Godrin: a wealthy noble house known for mana crystals, artifacts, arcane power, and a ruthless belief in the right to rule. Cassian recognized their white armor and banner at the tourney grounds. Source: 2026.05.05. House Wulfhelm: one of the most powerful houses in the Crownlands. They won last year's King's Tourney and currently hold the title and deed to the Thornwood Vale. Source: 2026.05.05. Jevon guided Odine Dunmere, Cassian, Aldrich, and Azrith into the city for the King's Tourney, then disappeared into the crowd. The party registered for the Proving Grounds as Cassian's Crushing Crusaders. They later discovered Jevon had been taken by House Godrin soldiers and found him tied up in the Stone Sanctum graveyard. After rescuing him and defeating a possessed knight, the party learned that House Godrin was interrogating Jevon about his teacher, a witch named Maralynn from the Thornwood Vale. See Rescue Jevon and Investigate the Pestilence. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.05.12.

The Gleaming Keep crowns the hill above Everdale. According to local lore, King Aldrich and his powerful mages transmuted the keep's stonework into metal so it would endure, causing it to gleam in the light. Source: 2026.05.05. The keep houses or protects the Empty Throne, which has remained unfilled since King Aldrich. The Oathkeepers guard the keep and preserve it for the hoped-for return of King Aldrich. The King's Tourney takes place in the valley below the keep. The party first entered on 2026.09.22. Oathkeepers guard its open metal doors and check visitors against a list. The walls were once pristine stonework, perhaps by master masons, dwarves or elves, and King Aldrich's archmages transmuted them into near-impenetrable steel. The halls hold ornate pews, banners and candelabra, but they are vast and empty, kept only by "bannerless knights" protecting the place from the noble houses. A chamber with a high porthole holds a teleportation circle tended by six Oathkeeper knights and a robed acolyte. It runs on spell draught and connects to other surviving circles from King Aldrich's era, including one in Havenport. See Oathkeepers. Source: 2026.09.22.

The King's Tourney is the annual tournament and festival held in the valley beneath Everdale and the Gleaming Keep. It lasts for about two weeks and draws noble houses, knights, merchants, performers, scouts, and spectators from across the Crownlands. Source: 2026.05.05. Proving Grounds: lower-tier competitions open to almost anyone who can pay the entry fee. Sponsors and scouts watch these bouts for promising talent. The fighting pit is 15 feet deep, dug straight into the earth—muddy, with craggy rocks underfoot, cheap banners overhead, and active betting rings running alongside. A noble box with a red tent sits above for scouts and midlords. Five levels of Crowd Favor are achievable; reaching Level 5 grants entry to the Grand Stage. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.06.02. Grand Stage: the main arena where top contenders, noble champions, and major bouts are held. Source: 2026.05.05. Registration tent: where entrants register for the tournament. Holt handled the party's registration. Source: 2026.05.05. Holt's registration tent for the Proving Grounds. Minnie's brewing stall (huckleberry mead from near the Thornwood Vale). Slug's cookhouse. Marea Voss' apothecary. Gruvelda Duskbelt's smithing commission tent. Source: 2026.05.12. Ragged Flagon: a makeshift tavern in the campgrounds where nobles don't typically go—recommended by Jevon as a safe place to lie low. Source: 2026.05.12. Cassian, Aldrich, Azrith, and Odine Dunmere entered the Proving Grounds as Cassian's Crushing Crusaders, won their first bout, then completed the Crown Gauntlet (started 2026.06.23, won 2026.07.14)—the first team to clear it in over seven years. The party has since advanced to The Menagerie, a beast-arena tier, with a bout scheduled 5 PM the day after 2026.08.11, red tent, bracketed near House Wulfhelm. Sponsored by Duke Tristan Blackwood (House Blackwood) at 8%. See Compete in the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.06.02, 2026.06.11, 2026.07.14, 2026.08.11. The tournament runs through ascending tiers of prestige and danger: Proving Grounds (entry-level bouts) → The Menagerie (beast-arena, judged on spectacle/daring/mastery) → Grand Stage (top contenders and noble champions). Crowd Favor levels within the Proving Grounds track toward this progression; the party's Crown Gauntlet win pushed them into the Menagerie tier directly. Source: 2026.08.11. Team competitions are common in the Proving Grounds, usually with groups of four. Magic is allowed. Higher-level competitors may use enchanted arms and armor. Strong performances can attract sponsors and possibly lead to the Grand Stage. The Crown Gauntlet—a 40-ft obstacle tower over a mud pit, scored via Cheer Marks/Mud Marks—was the Proving Grounds' obstacle-course format; the party's team is the first to clear it in over seven years. See Compete in the King's Tourney for full mechanics. The tourney's grand prize is the King's Cup together with a deed to the Thornwood Vale. Source: 2026.06.23. An unnamed, invitation-only "pleasure house" tent behind the theater near Slug's cookhouse is rumored to be frequented by nobles at night—identified but not yet visited by the party. Source: 2026.06.23. The three dominant houses at the tournament: House Godrin (arcane power, white armor), House Wulfhelm (militant, holds last year's deed), House Corwyn (knowledge seekers, silver armor). Vassal houses below these include House Blackwood (vassal of Corwyn; sponsoring the party), and others. The illegitimate House Oswall also arrives annually with a throne claim—they are considered a standing joke by established nobility.

The Ragged Flagon is a makeshift tavern set up in the campgrounds of the King's Tourney in Everdale. It caters to commoners and those who prefer to stay out of the notice of noble houses. Jevon recommended it to the party as a good place to lie low, noting that the nobles tend not to frequent it. Source: 2026.05.12. Recommended by Jevon after the fight at the Stone Sanctum as a safe lodging option. Run by Rory, an orc bartender. House ale is 1 silver per flagon—cheap, gut-rumbling, and effective. Gruvelda Duskbelt was spotted here by Azrith (natural 20 perception) the party's first night, hiding under a hood in a corner booth and keeping a very low profile. The Ragged Flagon is tent-only—no rooms to let. Participants with tourney registration have access to the free open campgrounds nearby. The party has since bought their own tent and campsite nearby (funded by Duke Tristan Blackwood's sponsorship money), making this area their base of operations. Source: 2026.08.11. Rory has now lost two bets against the party (their first Proving Grounds bout, then the Crown Gauntlet); Aldrich also stole an entire barrel of his mead undetected. Source: 2026.06.23, 2026.08.11.

The Stone Sanctum is an old stone cathedral in the hamlet of Everdale, above the King's Tourney on the hill. Unlike the whitewashed and painted buildings around it, it is bare stone, dark with age, and covered at its base in vines and moss. A bell hangs from its tower. The main entry opens onto a campus, and beyond the chapel building a cemetery occupies the grounds. Source: 2026.05.12. The interior is dim and musty—pews empty, candelabras unlit. The sign etched into the entry wall reads Stone Sanctum. A heavy door opens with an eerie creak. Iron candelabras line the walls, and stained glass windows look out toward the graveyard. Source: 2026.05.12. The party was led here by Azrith's supernatural senses and a high investigation roll (23) after Gruvelda Duskbelt told them that nobles had been seen meddling with magic in the hamlet cemetery. Inside the chapel, a scrap of green fabric caught on an iron candelabra was identified by Azrith as likely torn from Jevon's cloak, confirming Jevon had been brought here. In the graveyard, Odine Dunmere found Jevon bound in rope and tied to a cherubim statue, unconscious and bloodied. A dead black knight lay nearby. A second knight, possessed by an undead spirit (a ghoul), attacked the party. The possessed knight was defeated by the party; as the armor fell, a spectral form said "I submit, I must go" and dissipated. The dead knights were identified by Cassian as House Godrin foot soldiers. Two House Godrin bodies now lie in the graveyard. Source: 2026.05.12. Gruvelda Duskbelt's clan has heard rumors that some noble groups among the humans have been "messing around up in the hamlet, on the hill, in the cemetery." The Oathkeepers patrol the streets of the hamlet but apparently have not investigated the Sanctum themselves. The ghost that possessed the knight submitted willingly once defeated, suggesting these spirits may not all be malevolent by nature.

The Menagerie is the tournament tier above the Proving Grounds: a gladiatorial "fantasy bullfighting" arena where captured monsters are released into the ring for champions to fight, in front of thousands of spectators—far larger crowds than the Proving Grounds draws. Source: 2026.08.11. Posters advertise past creatures fought here: a steel-plated gorgon-bull, a medusa-type monster, and a griffon. Judged on spectacle, daring, and mastery, not just on killing the beast—per Holt: "any butcher can kill an animal." A bloodied, stretcher-carried adventurer was seen leaving the tent area, underscoring the increased danger over the Proving Grounds. Cassian's Crushing Crusaders advanced here after completing the Crown Gauntlet. Their bout is scheduled the day after 2026.08.11 at 5 PM, assigned the red tent, bracketed near a House Wulfhelm-affiliated opponent (red vs. blue tent). House Oswall also registered several unarmored entrants this year. Bouts here pit champions against released monsters rather than other champions directly. On 2026.08.25, Cassian's Unseen Servant scouted the previous bracket match—four black knights fighting a beast with a deep, lion-like roar, sketched by the servant as a manticore. The party then walked out to face a fresh manticore of their own; Odine's opening Intimidation check failed to faze it, and combat/initiative was deferred to the next session. Source: 2026.08.25. The manticore bout ended in an unprecedented way on 2026.09.08: rather than killing the beast, Cassian talked it down mid-combat, discovered it was a captive controlled by a trebuchet-and-net failsafe, and freed it—flying it to disable the trebuchet and letting it fly off unharmed. The arena's crowd-approval mechanic (a per-round d20 group check against a hidden DC) turned against the party as the fight dragged on without a kill; officials could not agree on how to score the bout, and the paying crowd largely booed, though peasants watching from a nearby cliffside outside the arena cheered the party as heroes. See The Freed Manticore. King's Tourney: The Menagerie is a tier within the overall tournament. Compete in the King's Tourney Holt: Registrar/leaderboard official who confirmed the promotion and judging criteria.

White Feather Tor is a tall, craggy hill in the Eastern Tourney Grounds, topped with white tents, flags, and banners and reached by a well-trodden natural path. It is the Godrin family camp—House Godrin's home base at the King's Tourney—and contains the Messenger Tent, the party's investigative target, as well as Golstang Godrin's central pavilion. Source: 2026.08.18. The front approach is heavily guarded: 4–5 knights, closed gates, high walls—identified (Perception, natural 20 by Odine Dunmere) as the worst way in. A sheer cliffside on another face of the hill offers a dangerous but viable nighttime climb to infiltrate unseen. A vague "marsh-lock lake approach" was also mentioned as a more overt alternative way to seek entry—not explored. The Messenger Tent, somewhere on the tor, is named in Duke Tristan Blackwood's intelligence note as a location tied to House Godrin's activity. Not yet entered. Successfully infiltrated on 2026.08.25 by Cassian and Azrith, both invisible (Cassian also flying). Azrith got in by shimmying up between two close-set gate pillars near the front gate. The Messenger Tent proved empty and locked down, but Azrith stole a guard's keyring and recovered an opened Godrin letter plus a strongbox with 73 gp and a potion of healing. Cassian eavesdropped on the main tent instead, overhearing Percival Godrin confirm Maralynn is alive. Cassian also spotted House Godrin's champion, Sir Thorin Cassavar ("the Crow"), patrolling the camp. Source: 2026.08.25. Central Pavilion — Golstang's seat; family business conducted here. Family Tents — Private quarters for the Godrin family. Arcane Pavilion — Warded and restricted. Messenger Tent — Correspondence and dispatches; the party's investigative target. Training Grounds — Ronan Godrin is frequently present here. Supply Wagons — The lightest-security area of the camp. 30 people total within the camp. 6–8 knights in distinctive matte-white Godrin armor. 12–15 men-at-arms in white-and-grey Godrin livery. Servants, messengers, grooms, and arcane attendants. Security is considerably higher after dark along the perimeter—but once past the perimeter guards, there's considerably more freedom to move about inside. Golstang Godrin — House patron. Stationed at the central pavilion. Heavily guarded. Percival Godrin — Frequently moves between the pavilion, Everdale, and the tourney grounds. Emberlee Godrin — Keeps mostly to the Godrin encampment. Rarely alone. Valerie Godrin — Regularly leaves camp. The most accessible Godrin away from the family. Ronan Godrin — Frequently found around the competitor and training grounds. House Godrin: This is their family camp; the tor and its Messenger Tent are tied to their activity. Duke Tristan Blackwood: Provided the intelligence note detailing this camp's layout and personnel. Investigate House Godrin: The tor is the target of the party's planned nighttime infiltration.

Havenport is a rain-lashed, decaying seaport on a rocky coast, reached by the party through the Oathkeepers' teleportation circle from the Gleaming Keep. Duke Tristan Blackwood sent the party here to lie low after the Menagerie manticore scandal, with orders to find Mauve Marigold and stay with her until he sends word. It is also Aldrich's home and shares his surname. Source: 2026.09.15, 2026.09.22. The town once held perhaps 1,000–5,000 people. Today it is nearly abandoned: ragged ships sit at the docks, farmland and village stretch behind, and the "city up above the rocky coastline" is mostly dark. Source: 2026.09.22. It has been in disarray since the fall of House Westermere, whose cliffside home, Westermere Manor, overlooks the town. Per Ian: "Seems like every time they solve one problem, two more crop up in its place." Source: 2026.09.22. The Wither is taking more and more of the weak and sick here. Source: 2026.09.22. Undead are infesting the ground beneath the manor. The survivors, including "Mav and her people," have taken refuge down in the village. Source: 2026.09.22. There is little literature in town for researching lore, "perhaps amongst the wealthy... but these people here are very much humble folk, survivors." Source: 2026.09.22. Westermere Manor: the ruined House Westermere keep on the cliffs. It holds the town's teleportation circle, guarded by Ian, and an undercroft where the ethereal and material planes are converging. The Salt House: a former warehouse in the shipyard from the town's heyday, now the survivors' community center and the only lit building in the village. Ian says they'll likely want coin for lodging, "but they aren't bad people." The party was heading there at the end of 2026.09.22. Aldrich's home: Ian treated Havenport as Aldrich's home, and Aldrich said he left roughly eight or nine years ago, "maybe longer." He admitted to "a little bit of a past there" but doesn't like to reminisce. He knew of House Westermere's fall. When the town was first named on 2026.09.15, the GM and Aldrich's player held a private aside; its content is not recorded. Source: 2026.09.15, 2026.09.22. Duke Tristan Blackwood: Sent the party here to lie low. Aldrich: His hometown and surname. Mauve Marigold: Blackwood's contact here. Not yet met. House Westermere: The town's fallen noble house. Oathkeepers: Maintain the town's teleportation circle.

Westermere Manor is the cliffside keep of the fallen House Westermere, overlooking Havenport. Like the Gleaming Keep, its walls were transmuted into metal, but here the metal is tarnished and neglected; the manor looks 10–15 years unkept. It holds Havenport's teleportation circle, watched by the lone Oathkeeper Ian. Beneath it is an undercroft where the ethereal and material planes are converging. Source: 2026.09.22. The circle is one of a few that survive from King Aldrich's time, linked to the Gleaming Keep's. To use it: Pour spell draught into the lines of the circle. Spell draught is a bluish-silver liquid transmuted from the Thornwood Vale mana crystals that House Godrin harvests. Hold the plate-sized metal keystone in the center of the circle. Speak the destination's name. Use of the circle is paid for with tribute to the Oathkeepers. Duke Tristan Blackwood paid roughly 5,000 gp for the party's trip. Ian took the keystone back when they arrived. Source: 2026.09.22. Stairwells on either side of the entrance hall lead down to the undercroft. Samantha Westermere, the family's ghost, says "much of it has fallen into the ethereal realm." Ian says undead are infesting it, and he keeps away with the help of an amulet. Village children sometimes wander up at night. Source: 2026.09.22. The Curtain: a floating sphere of swirling black mist blocking the archway from the first large room into a hallway. It whispered "door" to Odine Dunmere. Samantha calls it "a curtain to the realm of death," a passage between the ethereal and material planes. It opens and closes unpredictably and tends to close after it is used. Both the living and the dead use it, "some of them are vile." Traffic has grown as more people have died in recent years. Azrith leapt into it and vanished. See Find Azrith. The black veil: a shimmering black wall that has sealed off part of the undercroft since the Curtain opened. It wasn't there in Samantha's lifetime, and it is impenetrable to her. To a mortal it feels like cold steel. Black mist crawls up the arm and steals warmth, like entropy, "almost like it's turning your essence into living shadow." It is not evil in itself. It swallows light with no reflection. Radiant light (Odine's Sacred Flame) drives the shadow back. Cassian's magic check (natural 20) found that no one is casting a spell there. The wall itself is the source, and "whatever lies beyond that wall is affecting you." Samantha's room: where she died. House Westermere: The family that owned it. Samantha Westermere: Haunts the undercroft. Ian: The Oathkeeper posted at the circle. Havenport: The town below. Gleaming Keep: Linked by the teleportation circle.

The Thornwood Vale, usually just called "the Vale," is a forested valley behind the Gleaming Keep. It is the home of Odine Dunmere and her people, and the source of the blight known as the Wither (also called the pestilence or the hollowing). It is also the grand prize of the King's Tourney. The corruption there affects plants, animals and people, and it has now spread into the Crownlands. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.08.18. Naming note Speech-to-text usually writes "Vale" as "veil". A transcript audit (2026-09-25) confirmed that every place-reference to "the veil" in play means this Vale. That includes the home of Gruvelda Duskbelt's dwarven clan. The only literal "veil" so far is the black wall in the Westermere Manor undercroft. The Vale is a long, narrow forested canyon with black cliff sides and mountains rising to the east. From Everdale's hilltop it looks veiled in an almost imperceptible green mist. It was once the king's hunting grounds. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.05.12. The Guardians of the Vale: Odine's elven people, an isolated, matriarchal community. They stop aging while they remain in the Vale. There are "countless villages inside the Vale." See Odine Dunmere. Source: 2026.08.25. The Duskbelt dwarves: Gruvelda Duskbelt's clan lives in the Vale. Her brother Grimhall Duskbelt protects them from shadows and ghouls that "make their way down into the Vale," a problem he blames on the town above rather than the Vale itself. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.05.19. A dwarven clan that works with House Godrin supplies Godrin's mana crystals. It is not confirmed whether this is the Duskbelt clan. Source: 2026.06.23. Maralynn is from the Vale and is said to have "returned to her people in the Vale." House Godrin has confirmed she is alive. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.06.23, 2026.08.25. The tourney's grand prize is the King's Cup together with the deed and title to the Vale. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.06.11, 2026.06.23. House Wulfhelm won last year and holds the deed. It and House Godrin have traded the deed back and forth for about a decade. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.08.18. House Corwyn believes the Vale hides a secret that could unite the lesser houses against Godrin and Wulfhelm. Source: 2026.08.18. Mana crystals and spell draught: whoever holds the deed can mine the Vale's mana crystals. House Godrin uses them to power its arcane arsenal. They can also be transmuted into spell draught, the liquid that powers the Oathkeepers' surviving teleportation circles. Source: 2026.06.23, 2026.09.22. Odine insists "no one can hold the title to the Vale." Source: 2026.08.11. The pestilence is tied to the mist entity. Odine Dunmere's grandmother Mara, one of the Touched, sacrificed herself to cast the entity back. It is now as strong as it was then, and the blight is spreading faster than ever. Source: 2026.06.11. The humans' story of the King defeating the hollowing about 150 years ago is, in Odine's word, "Lies." Source: 2026.06.11. The kneeling statue: in the Oathkeepers' legend, all that was left of King Aldrich after he defeated the Dark King was "a statue of himself" in the Vale. Odine has seen it: a human king kneeling with his sword in the ground, alone in the forest. See Investigate the Pestilence. Source: 2026.09.22. Minnie's huckleberry mead is made from huckleberries harvested on the fringes of the Vale. Odine was surprised that people from Everdale risk going that close. Source: 2026.05.05. The corrupted horse the party met before reaching Everdale suggested the curse is no longer confined to the Vale. Source: 2026.05.05. Jevon has gone to an outpost on the Vale's western fringe to help mislead the House Godrin scouts chasing Odine's "Erendel Morath" decoy. The decoy's fake location is also deep in the Vale. Source: 2026.08.25, 2026.09.15. Investigate the Pestilence Odine Dunmere House Godrin, House Wulfhelm, House Corwyn Gruvelda Duskbelt, Grimhall Duskbelt Maralynn

Aldrich came to Everdale for the King's Tourney and had not personally visited the human capital before this session. Source: 2026.05.05. Aldrich is from a settlement "decently far" away that he described as somewhere between a town and a growing small city. Source: 2026.05.05. He once served as a soldier or security for a vassal house under House Wulfhelm. Source: 2026.05.05. He bought a bottle of Minnie's huckleberry mead and plans to save it for a victory celebration after the tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. He joined Cassian's Crushing Crusaders for the Proving Grounds. See Compete in the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. He recognized Kardis Wulfhelm as a prince of House Wulfhelm and made a joke about hoping Kardis's blade was not as sharp as his eyebrows. Source: 2026.05.05. After learning Jevon was taken, Aldrich wanted to look for a smithy before the group regrouped at sundown. Source: 2026.05.05. He took 4 necrotic damage from the possessed knight at the Stone Sanctum graveyard, reducing his max HP by 4 until a long rest. This was healed after sleeping in Boarhead Tor. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.05.19. He was awarded a Sentinel Shield by Gruvelda Duskbelt as payment for the ghost job: blue dwarven craftsmanship with an eye emblem, granting advantage on initiative rolls and perception checks. Requires an action to equip or stow—a trade-off between two-handed great sword offense and defensive shielded stance. Source: 2026.05.19. He contributes 1 gold to Cassian's 5-gold wager that the party wins their first bout without anyone being incapacitated. Aldrich gets free drinks from Cassian if they lose. Source: 2026.05.19. Aldrich keeps a mental book of prepared jokes and delivered one to the downed knight at the Stone Sanctum: "You picked a bad day to be ugly." Source: 2026.05.12. In the party's first Proving Grounds bout, Aldrich was the last party member standing while both Cassian and Azrith were downed. He used Evasive Footwork (Battle Master maneuver, expending 3 superiority dice) to disengage and boost his AC to 27 for a round. He landed a natural 20 Firebolt crit on one fighter (17 fire damage), applied his greatsword's Graze mastery for 5 slashing to fell the large frontliner, and claimed two knockouts. He quipped over the large enemy's downed body: "I expected more. That's on me." Source: 2026.06.02. Received Combat Greaves from Duke Tristan Blackwood's sponsorship delivery at Clover Hill: grants +5 ft of movement on the first round of each combat. Source: 2026.06.11. Registered the party for the Crown Gauntlet (obstacle course format); bout scheduled 7 PM, Tent A. Source: 2026.06.11. Visited Gruvelda Duskbelt's smithing tent to discuss lighter armor. Options presented: breastplate (250 gp, AC 17, no stealth disadvantage) or half plate (500 gp discounted from 750, AC 18, no stealth disadvantage). Decided to keep his current chain mail and forgo the upgrade. He accidentally called Gruvelda "Griselda"—she raised an eyebrow and gave him a hard look. Source: 2026.06.11. During the Crown Gauntlet, Cassian tossed Aldrich his Chain of the Unbroken mid-combat ("Catch, my friend!"); Aldrich used it through the rest of the challenge, though its full magical properties remain unidentified. Source: 2026.06.23.
