In the Gauntlet's conclusion, Aldrich burned his one Heroic Inspiration reroll to clear the sheer wall climb, took a natural-20 sack throw for 8 bludgeoning that nearly knocked him off a rotating platform (clawed back up), and helped haul Odine Dunmere to safety in the final rescue (a "Brutus drag" athletics check). Afterward he asked to retrieve a javelin he'd thrown and lost in the mud. Source: 2026.07.14. Received a +1 Greatsword bearing House Blackwood's crest as part of Duke Tristan Blackwood's Crown Gauntlet victory reward, delivered by his nephew Renny Blackwood. Source: 2026.08.11. Stole an entire barrel of mead from Rory at the Ragged Flagon via Sleight of Hand (rolled 19), completely undetected. Source: 2026.08.11. Commissioned upgraded armor from Gruvelda Duskbelt: blue-dyed, scale-shaped splint/plate armor for 200 gp (100 gp deposit paid, 8 hours to complete), replacing his worn chain mail. Source: 2026.08.11. During the long rest, Aldrich's private thoughts turned to what comes after the tourney—whether he'll stay with the party or whether everyone will go their own way once it's over. Source: 2026.08.11. Confirmed his former house as House Troth, a minor vassal of House Wulfhelm; served as rank-and-file guard/security, not nobility, and hails from "the seaside." Duke Blackwood advised keeping the connection quiet. Source: 2026.08.18. Won the King's Cup, Rory's weekly drinking tournament at the Ragged Flagon—out-drinking 18 rivals including a dwarf who died from the tournament's final round. Burned his Heroic Inspiration to survive the frost-giant liqueur round; ended the night at exhaustion level 6, functionally incapacitated. Reward: 90 gp and an oversized ornate brass drinking mug. Declared afterward: "I might have found my place in this world." Source: 2026.08.18. Treated overnight by Father Kaldus Vey at the King's Fair healer tents: repeated Greater Restoration castings (400 gp total, paid by the party) plus a long rest cleared his exhaustion from level 6 down to 2; he then slept through the following day to clear one more level, ending at exhaustion level 1 ahead of the Menagerie bout. Woke in borrowed Royal Chapel robes and fielded the priest's gentle questions about his "blood curse" tiefling heritage. Source: 2026.08.25. Finalized his commissioned splint armor (blue-dyed, scale-shaped) ahead of the Menagerie bout against a manticore. Source: 2026.08.25. In the manticore bout, missed both of his own sword swings (including a Heroic Inspiration reroll) while jumping at the airborne beast. Caught on to Cassian's plan to talk the manticore down and shoved Azrith out of melee with a natural-20 Athletics check to stop him attacking. Used Thaumaturgy's phantom sound and booming voice to whisper unsettling phrases into the judges' box, sowing confusion among the officials (Intimidation 9, called a moderate success). Tossed Azrith a healing potion after the bout. Source: 2026.09.08. Capped the escape from the Menagerie by casting Firebolt into the arena's outer tents and banners as a parting smokescreen. Praised by patrons at the Ragged Flagon afterward for the flair. Source: 2026.09.15. Reacted oddly when Duke Tristan Blackwood named their destination as Havenport—his own surname, known to him only from family bedtime stories. Held a private, undisclosed conversation with the GM about it; the connection to his backstory is unresolved. Source: 2026.09.15. Reached level 5, gaining Extra Attack. Source: 2026.09.15. Activated the Gleaming Keep's teleportation circle by holding the keystone and speaking "Havenport", after worrying aloud that he might leave parts of himself behind. In Havenport, the Oathkeeper Ian treated the town as Aldrich's home. Aldrich said he left roughly eight or nine years ago, "maybe longer," and admitted to "a little bit of a past there" that he doesn't like to revisit, including the fall of House Westermere. Led the party into the Westermere Manor undercroft. Source: 2026.09.22. Cassian: fellow member of the tourney team. Azrith: fellow member of the tourney team. Odine Dunmere: fellow member of the tourney team. House Wulfhelm: parent house of the vassal house Aldrich once served.

Azrith is energetic, curious, and easily drawn toward odd or spooky things. He traveled with the party into Everdale for the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. Azrith spent the morning at camp climbing trees while the rest of the group prepared to travel. Source: 2026.05.05. Marea Voss referred to him as her "horned friend," confirming Azrith has visible horns. Source: 2026.05.05. His background includes travel through the Crownlands among merchant or slaver routes, giving him some familiarity with the region but not necessarily with Everdale itself. Source: 2026.05.05. He joined Cassian's Crushing Crusaders for the Proving Grounds and signed the registration sheet with rough handwriting plus a note to "don't forget it." See Compete in the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. He noticed Jevon's magical box glinting in the muddy cart tracks after the party left Marea Voss' apothecary. See Rescue Jevon. Source: 2026.05.05. He misremembered Jevon's name as "Kevin," which became a table joke. Source: 2026.05.05. He caught Gruvelda Duskbelt's attention by using Thaumaturgy to conjure ghostly moans around her smithing tent, pitching the party as ghost hunters available to solve her problem. His persuasion roll (25) secured the deal. Source: 2026.05.12. His supernatural senses and a high investigation roll (23) led the party to the Stone Sanctum in the Everdale hamlet. Source: 2026.05.12. He has a Crimson Rite ability—specifically the Rite of Dawn. Activating it deals 1d4 necrotic damage to his own hand but grants resistance to necrotic damage, sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius, and adds bonus radiant damage against undead. His first known use was against the possessed knight at the Stone Sanctum. Source: 2026.05.12. He took a critical life drain hit from the possessed knight (natural 20), reducing his max HP to 12 until a long rest. This was fully healed after the long rest in Boarhead Tor. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.05.19. He finished the possessed knight with a magical scimitar strike, triggering the ghost's submission and dissipation. Source: 2026.05.12. He spotted Gruvelda Duskbelt hiding under a hood at the Ragged Flagon with a natural 20 perception roll, recognizing her despite the disguise. Source: 2026.05.19. He was awake while Cassian had his dream visit from The Masked Figure; Cassian covered for the dream by claiming he had dreamed about a woman. Source: 2026.05.19. In the party's first Proving Grounds bout, Azrith opened by casting Bless on three party members (1d4 bonus to all attack rolls and saving throws, 1-minute concentration), which carried the party through most of the fight. He landed Chill Touch (natural 20, 7 necrotic) and activated his Hematurgy. He was later critted for 21 slashing damage and incapacitated, dropping Bless. He made a successful death save (13). Cassian revived him with Healing Hands (6 HP, while using Azrith's horn as a handhold to get up). Azrith delivered the final blow with a Chill Touch natural 20 crit—placing a ghostly hand on the last fighter's chest, leaving a necrotic scar as the match was called. Source: 2026.06.02. The morning after the party's long rest, Azrith was absent—he had risen before sunrise without informing anyone. His whereabouts during that time are unknown. Source: 2026.06.11. Returned late the following night after "meeting with an old friend" (unelaborated). Odine Dunmere gave him her ill-fitting Clover Hill ring, which he took a liking to as a "Ring of Fire Breath"—a once-per-long-rest dragon-breath effect. Source: 2026.06.23. In the Crown Gauntlet's conclusion, Azrith was the skill-challenge MVP: a natural 1 followed by a natural 20 (with advantage) on Investigation let him coach the whole team through the sheer wall climb, and he later lowered Cassian's chain to rescue Odine Dunmere in the final round. He also used his Ring of Fire Breath improvisationally as an intimidation prop against a guard jamming the tower's gears (failed the check, but it still applied fire damage). Source: 2026.07.14. His full name was given for the first time as Azrith Duskrin. Source: 2026.08.11. Received Goggles of Night as part of Duke Tristan Blackwood's Crown Gauntlet victory reward: gnomish-crafted, fully conceal the wearer's eyes, and extend his darkvision to 120 feet. Used them to read that Jevon "seems scared about something... he's definitely hiding it." Source: 2026.08.11. Commissioned a new +1 scimitar built from scratch by Gruvelda Duskbelt for 400 gp (200 of his own gold + 200 from party funds), ready in 8–10 hours. Source: 2026.08.11. During the long rest, Azrith's private thoughts centered on helping the party reach its goals, alongside an unspecified personal goal of his own—not yet named. Source: 2026.08.11. Absent on 2026.08.18—the player was away, so per the established "ghost hunter" pattern, Azrith simply slipped out at night on unstated business, per Cassian: "he disappears every once in a while... probably sniffing rocks or picking flowers... but he's always on time." Did not appear on-page; no combat occurred that session requiring him to be piloted. Returned and infiltrated White Feather Tor alongside Cassian, invisible under Cassian's upcast spell. Shimmied up between two gate pillars (Acrobatics, failed then succeeded) to slip inside undetected. Reached the Messenger Tent, picked a guard's keyring with a rerolled Sleight of Hand (Heroic Inspiration, 23), opened a locked drawer to recover an already-broken-seal letter from House Godrin, and looted a strongbox for 73 gp and a potion of healing, taking the whole courier satchel. Source: 2026.08.25. In the Menagerie bout against the manticore, landed several hits (dagger and Chill Touch, including an opportunity attack) and cracked a fat joke at it mid-fight. Unaware Cassian had pivoted to talking the manticore down, kept attacking after it started to stand down—prompting Aldrich to physically shove him out of melee (natural 20 Athletics) to stop the fight from reigniting. Took 21 combined damage from the manticore's retaliatory rend attacks once it felt betrayed, but stayed standing (cushioned by an earlier False Life). Drank a healing potion Aldrich tossed him after the bout ended. Source: 2026.09.08. Privately conflicted about freeing the manticore—torn between wanting the fight and being "slapped on his ass" for continuing it once the party's plan changed—but said he thought they made the right choice regardless. Reached level 5, gaining Extra Attack and a +7 Perception modifier. Source: 2026.09.15. Absent on 2026.09.22; the GM ran him. Just before the teleport to Havenport he started to ask "hey wait, before we go, shouldn't we—" and was cut off. In the Westermere Manor undercroft he took a running jump into the Curtain, a sphere of black mist that is a passage to the realm of death, and vanished. He may return if he survives, whenever it reopens. See Find Azrith. Source: 2026.09.22. Jevon: Found his box after Jevon was taken; helped rescue him from the Stone Sanctum. Gruvelda Duskbelt: His ghost-hunter pitch won her over and secured the party's deal with her. Cassian, Aldrich, and Odine Dunmere: fellow members of the tourney team.

Cassian is familiar with Everdale, the King's Tourney, and several practical parts of the festival, including registration, food, and healing supplies. He often takes the lead when the party enters unfamiliar civic or noble territory. Source: 2026.05.05. Cassian noticed Odine Dunmere's violet pendant and the black tentacle-like marks on her arm while the party traveled toward Everdale. Source: 2026.05.05. He recognized House Godrin by its white armor and banner, and knows the house is wealthy, magically powerful, and ruthless. Source: 2026.05.05. His family house is a vassal of House Wulfhelm. He warned that interfering with guards or noble soldiers could create danger for the party and his family. Source: 2026.05.05. Cassian paid the 25 gold group entry fee for the party to compete as Cassian's Crushing Crusaders. See Compete in the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. He bought two healing potions from Marea Voss after haggling the price down. Source: 2026.05.05. He took custody of Jevon's magical box after Azrith found it in the road, then later agreed that Odine Dunmere could hold it. Source: 2026.05.05. His family signet ring is shaped like a falling star that meets its tail—ouroboros-like. It marks his house as old-blooded nobility, which carried weight with Gruvelda Duskbelt, who prefers old houses over new ambitious ones. Source: 2026.05.19. He carries magical dice that leave a burgundy trail when rolled. These were gifted to him by The Masked Figure in a prior dream. Source: 2026.05.19. He struck a deal with The Masked Figure during a dream on the night of the long rest: Cassian will keep the party together and Odine close; the Figure will remove tournament obstacles and find the origin of the dice. Source: 2026.05.19. He wagered 5 gold (his 4 plus 1 from Aldrich) that the party wins their first Proving Grounds bout without anyone being incapacitated. Standing to win 10 gold. Posing as an outside bettor. Source: 2026.05.19. He has met Kardis Wulfhelm in passing before and found him to be arrogant and reckless. Source: 2026.05.19. In the party's first Proving Grounds bout, Cassian activated Heavenly Wings (golden, once per long rest; adds 2d radiant to a spell or attack), flew 30 feet up, and fired Eldritch Blast on the enemy crossbowman for 8 force + radiant damage before Misty Stepping back down. The crossbowman returned fire with max damage (15 piercing), sending Cassian crashing to the mud and incapacitating him—1 death save failure. He was stabilized by Azrith's Spare the Dying, revived by Odine Dunmere's Healing Word (8 HP), and rose by using Azrith's horn as a handhold, casting Healing Hands on Azrith (6 HP) in the same motion. He also cast Phantasmal Force (a persistent dire wolf illusion area) and used a Luck point mid-fight. Source: 2026.06.02. The 5-gold wager is technically lost: the terms required no ally be knocked unconscious, and both Cassian and Azrith went down. Cassian plans to contest the loss with the coin master, arguing the party walked out on their feet. Source: 2026.06.02. After the first bout, Duke Tristan Blackwood (House Blackwood) made eye contact with Cassian from the noble box and gave a valiant golf-clap nod. Cassian winked back. Duke Blackwood is expected to approach as a potential sponsor. Source: 2026.06.02. Cassian's family house name is House Fortescue—confirmed when Virellan Le'Strange addressed him as "Lord Fortescue" at the tournament. House Fortescue's nature is celestial or semi-divine, descended from a bloodline cut off from the divine but still maintaining celestial heritage through the lineage. Source: 2026.06.11. Duke Tristan Blackwood formalized a sponsorship deal at 8% of any prize money, providing a 750 gp advance and four combat items. The party tried to negotiate down to 3% then 5% (persuasion with advantage, DC 22, rolled 14—failed); Blackwood would not go lower. Source: 2026.06.11. The 5-gp wager was formally lost. The Coin Master had already paid it out to Rory Greathorn (Rory) under the double-or-nothing clause (two party members were downed). No appeal was accepted. Source: 2026.06.11. Cassian received a Cloak of Protection (+1 AC and saving throws) from Duke Blackwood's sponsorship delivery at Clover Hill. He had it embroidered at the tailor: a falling star with an ouroboros crest and dust trail, matching his family signet ring. Cost: 8 silver. Source: 2026.06.11. Gruvelda Duskbelt gave Cassian a Chain of the Unbroken—10 feet of iron chain links, warm to the touch, held by Gruvelda for 250 years and described as having "a mind of its own." Cassian cast Identify and learned it has four properties (not yet disclosed). Source: 2026.06.11. An Insight check (18) during a long rest revealed House Godrin's core operation: they compete in the King's Tourney annually to harvest mana crystals via a dwarven clan in the Vale, fueling their armada and reinforcing their claim to the throne. Also confirmed: the tourney's grand prize is the King's Cup plus a deed to the Vale. Source: 2026.06.23. Attempted Friends on a House Corwyn knight guarding Clover Hill to gain entry—failed even after burning heroic inspiration to force a reroll. Tossed his Chain of the Unbroken to Aldrich mid-combat during the Crown Gauntlet. Received an ambiguous warning nod from Duke Tristan Blackwood about over-relying on flight and magic to bypass the course rather than physically overcoming it. Source: 2026.06.23. In the Gauntlet's conclusion, Cassian used Thaumaturgy to max the crowd's Cheer Marks (granting the party a stacking +1d4 on remaining rolls), reclaimed and used the mystery chain to free a jammed gear mechanism and rescue his allies, and fought the final tower guard directly with an improvised perfume-bottle "flamethrower," a Taunting Step teleport-and-goad, and a shove that knocked the guard off the platform. Delivered a bombastic victory speech naming Rory as a losing bettor. Source: 2026.07.14. Received the Eyes of Charming as part of Duke Blackwood's Crown Gauntlet victory reward: gilded spectacles granting three daily charges of Charm Person without spending a warlock spell slot (DC 13). Source: 2026.08.11. Noticed Gruvelda Duskbelt working black plate armor matching House Godrin's colors for unnamed paying clients; she neither confirmed nor denied arming Godrin, calling herself a neutral mercenary smith. Source: 2026.08.11. During the long rest, Cassian privately weighed whether freeing Jevon might cost him the tournament versus whether it might disrupt a noble power structure he sees as having abused the Vale for too long. When asked which outcome he'd prefer, he answered only: "Cassian will see where the wind takes him." Source: 2026.08.11. Confirmed to Duke Tristan Blackwood that House Fortescue has been a House Wulfhelm vassal for roughly 60 years—which visibly surprised Blackwood, who has never once heard Wulfhelm acknowledge the vassalage despite knowing many circles. Cassian deflected rather than explain: "There are few who remember us fondly... that is part of the reason I am here." Source: 2026.08.18. Received a sealed intelligence note from Blackwood listing names/locations tied to House Godrin's camp activity, plus a personal gift of an emberleaf cigar. Sponsored Odine Dunmere and Aldrich into the King's Cup drinking tournament (10–15 gp entry), won a 5 gp side bet from Rory backing Aldrich (Persuasion 18), and tried spraying perfume into Aldrich's mouth afterward in an attempt to revive him. Source: 2026.08.18. Paid Father Kaldus Vey 400 gp (materials plus donation) to treat Aldrich's exhaustion overnight. Infiltrated White Feather Tor invisible and flying (Celestial Revelation wings), eavesdropping on the camp's main tent; a History check identified the hushed voice as Percival Godrin's, overhearing confirmation that Maralynn is alive and has been located. Spotted House Godrin's champion, Sir Thorin Cassavar ("the Crow"), for the first time and avoided him. Brought the intercepted Godrin letter to Duke Tristan Blackwood, prompting Blackwood to suspect a mole in his own camp. Studied his Eyes of Charming in his downtime. Source: 2026.08.25. Freed the manticore during the Menagerie bout instead of killing it: cast Sleep on it mid-flight to open the fight, then talked it down over several rounds (Persuasion checks of 23 and a near-crit 25), learning it feared its true captors' trebuchet-and-net failsafe more than the party. Mounted it, flew to the trebuchet, cast Charm Person (DC 13) on its operator to stand him down, and let the manticore destroy the machine. Delivered a booming public speech framing the outcome as a beast choosing freedom over bloodsport, backed by a follow-up Persuasion check (22) that won over only part of the crowd—officials were furious and unable to agree on a score, and Duke Tristan Blackwood was seen quietly avoiding eye contact while trying to leave the box. See The Freed Manticore. Source: 2026.09.08. Met Captain Garan and Lady Elwyn Blackwood for the first time en route to an urgent audience with Duke Blackwood. In private, Blackwood dropped his stern facade and called the manticore stunt "fucking genius"—furious about the gold spent but delighted that the scandal makes the party "the perfect distraction" from his other dealings. Warned soberly that mercy will eventually cost lives, and that the party had better be right whenever they place their own judgment above his orders. Escorted out of the fairgrounds by Captain Garan to Havenport to let tensions cool, since Blackwood couldn't reward them monetarily while recouping his gambling losses. Source: 2026.09.15. Reached level 5. Source: 2026.09.15. Awed on his first visit inside the Gleaming Keep (Perception 23). In Havenport, the Oathkeeper Ian recognized him as "Lord Fortescue's son" ("Well, so they say," Cassian answered). This is the first person in a long time to remember House Fortescue. Rolled a natural 1 on Arcana against the Curtain, and a natural 20 on his magic check against the black veil, finding that the wall itself is the source and that something beyond it reaches through. Flirted with the ghost Samantha Westermere and promised to return: "A Fortescue always keeps their promise." Source: 2026.09.22. Odine Dunmere: Cassian noticed signs of her connection to the pestilence, but left the matter alone. Now under an obligation to keep her at the tournament and close to the group. Aldrich and Azrith: registered with Cassian for the tourney. Jevon: Cassian returned Jevon's box during combat and is cautious about further entanglement. Slug: Cassian has eaten at Slug's cookhouse before and remembered the pork fondly. The Masked Figure: A mysterious patron who appears in Cassian's dreams and has struck a deal with him. House Wulfhelm: Cassian's family house is a vassal of Wulfhelm, giving him access to their camp area but also obligations. Duke Tristan Blackwood (House Blackwood): Noticed Cassian's performance at the first Proving Grounds bout; expected to approach as a potential sponsor.

Odine Dunmere is a 25-year-old half-elf from the Thornwood Vale. As of 2026.09.15 she is a level 5 Sorcerer 3 / Warlock 2. Where her warlock power comes from has not been named in play. Source: 2026.09.15. Odine comes from an ancient elven line. Her grandmother married a human, and her mother, Elira Dunmere, later married a half-elf named Etienne in an attempt to keep the bloodline balanced. These details come from Odine's written backstory and have not yet come up at the table. Her mother is alive and has already outlived Odine's grandmother. Much of her family still lives in the Vale, and their home holds several of the Vale's old straw dolls. Source: 2026.06.11. Odine describes her family as "a long line of witches... powerful magic casters who somehow are immune to this but still show symptoms," and her people as elves "who just wish to be left alone and fade into history." Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.08.25. Her grandmother Mara died at 71, long before Odine was born. She "sacrificed herself in the most painful way" to cast the entity back. Gruvelda Duskbelt, who knew Mara from girlhood, says most humans no longer remember that sacrifice. Odine believes the entity is now as powerful as it was when Mara drove it back. Source: 2026.06.11. Unresolved Gruvelda said she "never knew Mara to have any children," which sits uneasily with Mara being Odine's grandmother. This has not been explained at the table. Source: 2026.06.11. Odine is one of the Touched, the lineage that bears the burden of holding the entity back. Gruvelda recognized her as Touched on sight and said the Touched's lifespans have been shrinking with each generation, until she feared none remained. Odine calls herself "the youngest" and admits she has not had enough time among the Touched to learn how to use their power or to bind the entity alone. Source: 2026.06.11. Black, tentacle-like marks run from her wrists up both arms. She told Jevon she has carried them for "about 15 years," and he found it impossible that her mind was still intact after so long. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.05.12. Her magic is not fully under her control. Fear, shock or stress can make it surge on its own: she once cast an involuntary Message into Gruvelda's mind, and her Eldritch Blasts "erupt" from her hands. When she lets the Touched power through, her eyes turn fully black and mist pours from her body. Gruvelda told her she needs "a good teacher, someone who understands how to control the arcane power that resides within you." Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.06.02, 2026.06.11, 2026.08.25. Odine loves the Vale and its people. But among them, half-elves are treated as a lower class who would never lead a village. That prejudice sharpened once she was known to be Touched, because the Vale must now trust a half-human descendant with the role of binder and protector. Source: 2026.05.05. Violet crystal pendant: of deep personal importance. It has been fused with the Shadowfell Shard from Duke Tristan Blackwood's Gauntlet reward, and it glows when she channels Metamagic. She clutches it when frightened. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.08.11, 2026.09.08, 2026.09.22. Village charm: a charm marking her home village, which hung on the same necklace. She gave it to Duke Blackwood as the token backing her "Erendel Morath" decoy. Source: 2026.08.25. Many of her people now bear the mark, the crops are failing, and she is "the one tasked to deal with this." The blight is spreading "faster and faster" and has reached the Crownlands. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.06.11, 2026.08.18. She knows that the humans' story of their King defeating the hollowing about 150 years ago is a lie. On 2026.09.22 she recognized the Oathkeepers' legend of the Dark King as "very similar to those of my family," and remembered once finding the statue of King Aldrich kneeling alone in the Vale's forest. Source: 2026.06.11, 2026.09.22. She hopes to find someone powerful enough to teach her, to master her power faster, and to bind or seal the entity again, ideally forever. She insists that "no one can hold the title to the Vale." Source: 2026.06.11, 2026.08.11. Odine's people rarely leave the Thornwood Vale because the forest is, for elves, nearly perfect. The Vale's forest holds a power beyond their full understanding. After the elves arrived there about 1,300 years ago, they stopped aging and even returned to youthful bodies. The elders who first settled the Vale still live there. (This comes from Odine's written backstory. In play she has said the blight has worsened "over the last thousand years.") Source: 2026.06.11. The Vale's immortality is conditional. If someone leaves, the gift ceases and their age can accelerate rapidly. Only younger elves under about 50 years old can leave safely, and even they must return within a few years or their lives begin to fade. The community remains isolated, though the men of the Vale sometimes leave to trade. The people call themselves the Guardians of the Vale. The Guardians are matriarchal. Men are considered equals, but women naturally lead because of their ties to the magic of the Vale forest. Odine carries a violet pendant that appears deeply important to her. Cassian noticed this while traveling to Everdale. Source: 2026.05.05. The corrupted horse outside the Vale has made Odine fear that the entity's curse is spreading beyond the place she thought it was bound to. She is overwhelmed by Everdale and its customs, including meat-heavy city food and mead. Source: 2026.05.05. Her reaction to Kardis Wulfhelm reflects the lower status half-elves hold in her home culture and the fact that half-elves would not normally lead there. Source: 2026.05.05. She reluctantly joined the King's Tourney team, Cassian's Crushing Crusaders, despite not wanting to fight at first. See Compete in the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. She met Gruvelda Duskbelt, a dwarven smith who survived the same curse by amputating her own hand. Odine uncontrollably cast Message into Gruvelda's mind when she saw Gruvelda's preserved severed hand—a rare instance of her power acting without her conscious intent. She then revealed her own arm markings to Gruvelda. Gruvelda agreed to speak with her in detail after the first week of the festival. Source: 2026.05.12. She used her innate sorcery in combat at the Stone Sanctum graveyard, casting Sorcerous Burst (lightning/thunder damage, 13 total, halved to 6 against the ghoul's resistance) with advantage and a +7 to attack. Her power surged when she feared for her companions. Source: 2026.05.12. She freed Jevon from his rope bindings at the Stone Sanctum by trading her action to saw through the ropes. She healed him with Healing Word (9 HP) before freeing him. Source: 2026.05.12. She holds one of two communication stones enchanted by Jevon. She can send him one short message and receive a telepathic reply. She is to use it at night when the party has a safe meeting place. Source: 2026.05.12. She recognized Jevon's magical box as ancient elven craftsmanship—a relic, not a common trinket. Source: 2026.05.12. In the party's first Proving Grounds bout, Odine cast Witch Bolt (24 to hit, 9 lightning damage), creating a visible arc to an enemy. She used Innate Sorcery (bonus action) to gain advantage on attack rolls for sorcerer spells and boost her spell save DC. She goaded an enemy attack to draw it off Cassian, cast Armor of Agathus (5 temp HP; 5 cold damage to any melee attacker), and later re-cast it. After Cassian was revived, she discharged Witch Bolt as a bonus action (8 lightning), electrocuting an enemy into the ground. She ended the session casting Healing Word to revive Cassian (8 HP). Her magic came across as partly uncontrolled—she roleplayed an Eldritch Blast as erupting involuntarily from stress. Source: 2026.06.02. Received a Ring of Scorching Ray from Duke Tristan Blackwood's sponsorship delivery at Clover Hill; usable once per long rest. Source: 2026.06.11. While retrieving Cassian's cloak from the tailor, Odine noticed a wooden straw doll on the seamstress's dresser (Perception 15). Insight 22 revealed it had been given to the seamstress by Gruvelda Duskbelt when the seamstress's mother died. History 19 revealed the doll was approximately 100 years old and originated from Odine's home region—the Thornwood Vale. The seamstress gave it to Odine freely. This doll belonged to the same cultural and magical heritage as Odine's family. Source: 2026.06.11. At Gruvelda Duskbelt's smithing tent, Odine presented the doll (natural 20 persuasion). Gruvelda revealed she had personally known Mara, Odine's grandmother—they met by the river when Gruvelda was young, collecting geodes, and became long friends. Gruvelda said Mara "sacrificed herself" in a way that "is no longer remembered by most humans." Gruvelda told Odine: "You have been touched. Mara told me about your lineage and the burden you've borne." The lifespans of the Touched have been dwindling; Gruvelda feared none might remain. She confirmed the hollowing is spreading faster and has begun appearing in the Crown Lands. The king's reputed victory over it 150 years ago was, in Odine's words, a lie. Source: 2026.06.11. Gruvelda gave Odine an Elven Chain (mithril chainmail undershirt of elven craftsmanship, not Gruvelda's own making): "Wear it beneath your clothes. It will protect you." Source: 2026.06.11. Her Ring of Scorching Ray from Clover Hill wouldn't attune correctly; she gave it to Azrith, who used it as a "Ring of Fire Breath" (dragon-breath effect)—a discrepancy from the ring's original identification that remains unreconciled. During the Crown Gauntlet, she cast Tasha's Hideous Laughter and a Silent Image illusory owlbear that routed two obstacle guards. Source: 2026.06.23. In the Gauntlet's conclusion, Odine restrained a guard with Mold Earth, used Gust and a deliberately low Fog Cloud tactically, and landed two Eldritch Blasts (Repelling Blast)—drawing on her warlock levels. She closed the fight by casting Healing Word on the guard she'd just blasted unconscious, out of guilt. Source: 2026.07.14. Received a Shadowfell Shard as part of Duke Tristan Blackwood's Crown Gauntlet victory reward, and fused it onto her existing crystal pendant: as a spellcasting focus, using it with a Metamagic option lets her curse a targeted creature with disadvantage on checks/saves of one chosen ability score. Source: 2026.08.11. Bought two Potions of Greater Healing (280 gp) from Marea Voss. Continues to support Jevon in hiding via the sending stone, including a 50 gp and mead cache left at a hidden drop point. Source: 2026.08.11. During the long rest, Odine reflected on feeling far from her family in the Thornwood Vale but grounded by the friends around her. Source: 2026.08.11. Gave Duke Tristan Blackwood her most direct explanation yet of her mission—"from beyond the Vale," seeking to save her homeland from a crop-killing blight. Blackwood confirmed the blight has spread into the Crownlands themselves. Source: 2026.08.18. Scouted White Feather Tor with a natural-20 Perception check, identifying a viable nighttime cliffside infiltration route to the Messenger Tent tied to House Godrin. Entered the King's Cup drinking tournament, rigged a side bet against her own success (Deception 14), reached exhaustion level 2, vomited, and bowed out. Cast Spare the Dying on Aldrich reflexively after his final failed save. Source: 2026.08.18. Cleared her own exhaustion down to level 1 via a long rest alongside Aldrich's treatment. Helped bring the intercepted Godrin letter to Duke Tristan Blackwood and, on the spot, improvised a decoy to protect Maralynn: a fabricated name (Erendel Morath) and a false location deep in the Thornwood Vale, backed by her own home-village charm pendant—removed from her necklace and handed to Blackwood—to make the lead convincing. Blackwood agreed to float it through his own channels as misdirection. Source: 2026.08.25. In the manticore bout, landed a quickened Mind Sliver and a Thunderwave (16 thunder, halved on a successful Con save). When Cassian pivoted to freeing the manticore, cast Cause Fear on the loudest heckler in the crowd (failed save) to sow panic and distract the officials, publicly condemning the spectacle as "cold-blooded murder, not a test"—drawing a "she's a witch!" shout from the stands. Cast an illusory bowing manticore (Silent Image) in solidarity once the beast was freed. Source: 2026.09.08. Read Lady Elwyn Blackwood with an Insight check (13) as a sharp social manipulator, distinct from her husband's strategist style. Grew wary of the camp's unfamiliar faces after the day's fallout and proposed the party start keeping night watches or find more secure lodging. Messaged Jevon via her sending stone to let him know the party was heading to Havenport. Kept first watch that night (Perception 19, safe), taking on an extra point of exhaustion for it. Reached level 5 (Sorcerer 3 / Warlock 2); the GM pointed out her unusually high Deception and Intimidation modifiers go underused, prompting her to lean into a deliberately "naive-seeming but actually shrewd" persona going forward. Source: 2026.09.15. In Havenport, heard the Oathkeeper Ian's legend of the Dark King and remembered once finding the statue of King Aldrich kneeling with his sword in the ground, alone in the Vale's forest: "I've seen this statue that you speak of with my own eyes." She said the tale is very similar to her family's stories. Spoke telepathically with the Curtain, which answered "door". Her History check (14) sensed that the black veil is foreign, non-elven magic where the ethereal and material planes are converging. She touched it and drove back its creeping shadow with Sacred Flame, and warned Cassian telepathically. Believes she can figure out the wall. Source: 2026.09.22. Cassian noticed her pendant and the black tendril marks but did not press her. Marea Voss warned Odine to seek true sources about the pestilence and avoid those who exploit misinformation. Gruvelda Duskbelt: Fellow survivor of the corruption (Gruvelda by amputation). She knew Odine's grandmother Mara and recognized Odine as Touched. A key ally in the pestilence investigation. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.06.11. Jevon: Rescued him at the Stone Sanctum. Holds his communication stone. His teacher Maralynn is from the Thornwood Vale and may be connected to the pestilence. Mara: her grandmother, a Touched binder who sacrificed herself to cast the entity back. She died at 71. Elira Dunmere: her mother, alive in the Thornwood Vale and older than Mara lived to be. Etienne: her father, per her written backstory. He has not been mentioned in play. Investigate the Pestilence Rescue Jevon Compete in the King's Tourney

Captain Garan is Duke Tristan Blackwood's captain of the guard—a decorated soldier the party had not met before. He approached them with haste (though not overt aggression) shortly after the Menagerie bout, warning them cryptically: "You wagered and you lost. But you're only wagering against a prize. The duke is wagering against his name." He advised them to "be careful the games you play. You don't know what you've set off." Source: 2026.09.15. Per Lady Elwyn Blackwood, his tension isn't really about the party—he worries about the loyalty of his men, some of whom are paid mercenaries who could "swear fealty elsewhere" if frightened. She considers him "perfectly capable" and somewhat prone to overreacting. Ordered by Duke Blackwood to escort the party safely out of the fairgrounds to Havenport and to "see that they understand what comes next." Did not acknowledge Cassian's pleasantries before leading the party out. Told the party to report back to him in the morning. Met the party at dawn at the Blackwood camp, rebuffed Cassian's attempted hug ("just personal space, man"), and escorted them to the Gleaming Keep. There he paid roughly 5,000 gp of Blackwood's money in tribute and handed over the spell draught for the teleportation circle. It is not recorded whether he teleported with them to Havenport. Source: 2026.09.22. Duke Tristan Blackwood: His liege and employer; entrusted with the party's safety and departure. Lady Elwyn Blackwood: Speaks of him with familiarity and mild indulgence.

Duke Tristan Blackwood is a midlord of House Blackwood, a vassal house that holds a smaller parcel of land loaned to them by one of the greater houses. House Blackwood is not one of the big three noble houses at the King's Tourney and does not typically win tournaments. Source: 2026.06.02. Present at the King's Tourney. During the party's first Proving Grounds bout, he walked from the noble box to the table with his goblet and began watching mid-fight. After the bout ended he gave Cassian a golf-clap acknowledgment and a valiant nod when their eyes connected. Cassian winked back. Following the bout, he formalized a sponsorship deal: 8% of any prize money in exchange for a 750 gp advance and four combat items (delivered at Clover Hill). The party attempted to negotiate down to 3% then 5% (persuasion with advantage, DC 22, rolled 14—failed); Duke Blackwood would not go lower than 8%. Source: 2026.06.02, 2026.06.11. His level of nobility is comparable to Cassian's family house—approachable, not a high lord. Watches from a red-tent section of the noble box at the Proving Grounds. He did not pay close attention to the match until partway through, when the fighting quality drew him in. House Blackwood is a vassal of House Corwyn, one of the three dominant houses at the tournament. Duke Blackwood operates within Corwyn's sphere of influence. Source: 2026.06.11. Gruvelda Duskbelt's assessment of him is blunt: "Backwood—slimy bastard. Stay away from him." The party is now bound to his sponsorship despite this warning. Source: 2026.06.11. Agreed to dig through his House Corwyn contacts for intelligence on House Godrin's weaknesses—contingent on the party performing well in the Crown Gauntlet. Source: 2026.06.23. Watched the party complete the Crown Gauntlet from the sponsor's box with only a slow, reserved clap—"amused and amazed" rather than jubilant, a notably muted reaction to his own sponsored team's biggest win yet. Source: 2026.07.14. Sent his nephew and manservant, Renny Blackwood, to deliver the Gauntlet victory reward (1,500 gp split among the party plus individualized magic items) along with an invitation to visit his tent that evening "to discuss business"—not yet acted on. Source: 2026.08.11. Finally hosted the party at his tent on 2026.08.18: found with muddy boots up on his desk, smoking an "emberleaf" cigar (mundane relaxant, no magic). Dismissed his guards for privacy and asked each PC's origin story. Visibly surprised that Cassian's house, House Fortescue, is a House Wulfhelm vassal—he's never once heard Wulfhelm acknowledge them despite running in many circles, and pressed the point without getting a straight answer. Confirmed the blight/pestilence has spread beyond the Thornwood Vale into the Crownlands themselves, supplying the word "blight" himself when Odine described it obliquely. Delivered a major lore dump on the tournament's true stakes: House Godrin and House Wulfhelm have traded the Vale's deed between them for 10 years; House Corwyn (his own liege house) believes the Vale hides a secret that could unite the lesser houses against Godrin and Wulfhelm. He personally would enjoy seeing all three great houses lose this year—unprecedented in a century. Framed the party's edge as "nobody owns you," distinct from being sponsored. Warned that House Godrin has been unusually active and is rumored to be kidnapping children; revealed that as a young competitor he personally witnessed Godrin abducting hedge mages, and wonders what frightened "one of the most powerful arcane families in the Crownlands" into resorting to kidnapping. Gave Cassian a sealed intelligence note (names/locations tied to Godrin's camp activity) and a second emberleaf cigar as a gift. Advised investigating at night. Source: 2026.08.18. Reacted with visible alarm on 2026.08.25 when shown a letter recovered from House Godrin's camp: he only knows the name Marlin (Maralynn) from folklore—an archmage who served King Aldric the Wise, presumed dead since "the ancient war." Concluded from the letter's contents that he has a mole in his own camp feeding House Godrin information, admitting he had "flirted with one of their nieces." Agreed to float a decoy name and location (Odine Dunmere's fabrication, "Erendel Morath," backed by her family charm pendant) through his own intelligence channels to mislead Godrin. Source: 2026.08.25. When Cassian freed the Menagerie's manticore instead of killing it—turning the crowd and officials against the party—Blackwood was seen quietly trying to slip out of the noble box, avoiding eye contact with the party for the first time. His reaction to sponsoring a team that just publicly disrupted the tournament is unresolved. Source: 2026.09.08. Privately delighted by the outcome once alone with the party: drew a dagger dramatically before admitting "that was fucking genius." Chastised them for the gold spent but conceded their unplanned solution serves him better than anything he could have designed—the scandal makes the party "the perfect distraction" from his other dealings. Warned that mercy will eventually cost lives, and that the party must be prepared to answer for placing their own judgment above his orders. Unable to reward them financially while recouping his gambling losses, he sent them to Havenport under Captain Garan's escort to let tensions cool. His wife, Lady Elwyn Blackwood, separately told the party she welcomed the change of pace. Source: 2026.09.15. Per the GM's recap, he also ordered the party to find Mauve Marigold in Havenport and stay with her until he sends word. He secured Oathkeeper permission for the Gleaming Keep's teleportation circle and paid roughly 5,000 gp in tribute through Captain Garan. Source: 2026.09.22. House Blackwood: His house, for which he serves as duke/midlord. House Corwyn: His liege house—though he's privately a wildcard rather than a loyal partisan. Cassian: Made eye contact with Cassian after the first bout; appears interested in the party's potential; suspicious of Cassian's evasiveness about House Fortescue. Renny Blackwood: His nephew and manservant/courier. Captain Garan: His captain of the guard. Lady Elwyn Blackwood: His wife.

Emberlee Godrin is a member of House Godrin's ruling family, named in Duke Tristan Blackwood's intelligence note on the Godrin camp at White Feather Tor. She keeps mostly to the encampment and is rarely alone—making her a difficult infiltration target compared to other family members. Source: 2026.08.18. House Godrin: Family member. Golstang Godrin: Presumed relative (patron). White Feather Tor: Rarely leaves the camp.

Father Kaldus Vey is a middle-aged priest of the Royal Chapel working the healer tents at the King's Fair. He treated Aldrich's exhaustion after the King's Cup, casting Greater Restoration (capped at three castings per day) for a fee of 100 gp in diamond dust plus a 300 gp materials cost, sweetened by a 100 gp donation from Cassian—400 gp total. Source: 2026.08.25. Warm and welcoming, quick to invite passersby in "to pray." Cares for patients overnight in his sanctuary; made Aldrich a makeshift bed and dressed him in spare Royal Chapel robes after his ruined clothes were discarded. Curious about Aldrich's tiefling heritage, gently probing about his "blood curse" (red skin, horns) and offering a "path of redemption" without pressing when Aldrich brushed it off. Mentioned that House Oswall clerics have recently moved into the fairgrounds as an alternative option, and that tournament healers exist but are normally gated behind noble access or steep fees. Aldrich: Treated his exhaustion over the course of a night and morning. Cassian: Negotiated payment with him directly.

Golstang Godrin is the current patron of House Godrin. He has not appeared directly, but Cassian knew his house by reputation when the party reached the King's Tourney. Source: 2026.05.05. Per Duke Tristan Blackwood's intelligence note, he's stationed at the central pavilion of the Godrin family camp at White Feather Tor (Eastern Tourney Grounds)—heavily guarded. Source: 2026.08.18. House Godrin: Patron of the house. White Feather Tor: His camp and pavilion. Percival Godrin, Emberlee Godrin, Valerie Godrin, Ronan Godrin: Fellow Godrin family members named in Blackwood's note.

Grimhall Duskbelt is Gruvelda Duskbelt's brother and a dwarven lord of the Duskbelt clan, whose home is in the Thornwood Vale. He is responsible for protecting his clan from the shadows and ghouls that "make their way down into the Vale," a problem he believes originates in the town above (Everdale) rather than in the Vale itself. Source: 2026.05.19. Not yet encountered. Gruvelda recommended the party seek him out if they ever travel to the Vale, saying he may have work and coin for true ghost hunters. Source: 2026.05.19. Gruvelda passed word to him that the party handled the ghost problem at the Stone Sanctum in Everdale. The shadows and ghouls troubling his clan may be connected to the same supernatural forces the party encountered at the Stone Sanctum. He is characterized by Gruvelda as someone who does not hand out coin lightly and will need proof of results. Gruvelda Duskbelt: His sister. She vouches for the party to him. Cassian, Aldrich, Azrith, Odine Dunmere: Prospective ghost hunters he may hire.

Gruvelda Duskbelt is a dwarven master smith and one of the only dwarves at the King's Tourney. She is older, stout, and gruff, with reddish-tinged skin and a massive fur cloak she wears even while working the forge. She runs a high-demand smithing commission tent at the fair, preferred by noble houses, and takes on orders from a position of power—she turns away those who cannot meet her standards or pay. Source: 2026.05.12. Present at the King's Tourney but keeping a very low profile. She was spotted at the Ragged Flagon by Azrith (natural 20) while hiding under a hood. She has delivered the reward for the ghost job. In session 2026.06.11, Odine Dunmere visited her smithing tent with the wooden straw doll—Gruvelda opened up and spoke at length about Mara, the hollowing, and her true purpose at the tournament. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.05.19, 2026.06.11. She is one of a very small number of dwarves at the King's Tourney, which she explains by saying she sees humans purely as a source of gold. She carries two hammers and works forging hot plate as standard labor while managing high-profile noble commissions. Her clan is from the Vale. Her brother, Grimhall Duskbelt, protects the clan from the shadows and ghouls that "make their way down into the Vale." She survived the same corruption that afflicts Odine Dunmere and the Thornwood Vale by severing her own hand. She now wears a prosthetic on her right arm and keeps the dried, corrupted hand in a small wooden box on her shelf as a reminder or trophy. She bears no ill will toward humans as a rule but has heard her clan's stories about "sniveling humans" meddling with magic in the Everdale hamlet cemetery, which she finds distasteful. When Azrith used Thaumaturgy to conjure ghostly sounds near her tent as a calling card, she was not startled—she recognized it as a pitch. She bought it, gave the party extra time, and struck a deal. She told Odine bluntly: "None of these people here know what's coming." She is at the King's Tourney to observe—not to serve any of the noble houses, but to watch them fight over the Thornwood Vale deed and learn. Source: 2026.06.11. She personally knew Mara, Odine Dunmere's grandmother. They met when Gruvelda was young, by the river while she was collecting geodes. Mara was "kinder than I thought her people to be." They became long friends. Mara "sacrificed herself—a sacrifice no longer remembered by most of these humans." Source: 2026.06.11. She gave Odine Dunmere a wooden straw doll to a seamstress at the tailor tent years prior (when the seamstress's mother died); the doll was originally from Thornwood Vale and 100 years old—likely connected to Mara. Source: 2026.06.11. Her view of Duke Tristan Blackwood: "Backwood—slimy bastard. Stay away from him." Source: 2026.06.11. Aldrich accidentally called her "Griselda" once; she gave him a sharp eyebrow and a hard look. Source: 2026.06.11. On 2026.08.11, Cassian noticed her working black plate armor matching House Godrin's colors for unnamed paying clients; she neither confirmed nor denied it, framing herself as a neutral mercenary smith who "armors all of the knights in this realm." When Odine asked about Jevon's pursuers, she quietly revealed a key lead: House Godrin keeps detailed ledgers of all their activity at an outpost on the outskirts of the fair. She commissioned upgraded armor for Aldrich (blue-dyed scale/plate, 200 gp, 8 hours) and a new +1 scimitar built from scratch for Azrith (400 gp, 8–10 hours). Source: 2026.08.11. Gruvelda's ghost-job deal is complete. She was persuaded of the party's success (Cassian's persuasion + Aldrich's assistance, result 12; sealed when Cassian revealed his old-house signet ring). She delivered: A Sentinel Shield for Aldrich: blue-painted dwarven craftsmanship with an eye emblem. Grants advantage on initiative rolls and perception checks. Requires an action to equip or stow. 4 gold coins each for all four party members. A lead: her brother Grimhall Duskbelt in the Vale, who may have work and coin for ghost hunters. She has passed word to him about the party. Source: 2026.05.12, 2026.05.19. At her smithing tent, after Odine Dunmere produced the wooden straw doll (nat 20 persuasion), Gruvelda gave two items unprompted: Elven Chain → Odine Dunmere: mithril chainmail undershirt of elven craftsmanship (not Gruvelda's own making). "Wear it beneath your clothes. It will protect you." She had been saving it for the right moment. Chain of the Unbroken → Cassian: 10 feet of iron chain links, warm to the touch, held by Gruvelda for 250 years and described as having "a mind of its own." Cassian cast Identify and learned the chain has four properties (not disclosed in session). Source: 2026.06.11. Aldrich: She sized him up as the strong one of the group and made her deal with him directly. Azrith: His ghost-hunter pitch using Thaumaturgy caught her attention. Cassian: She found his charm amusing but unconvincing on its own; she dragged him out of the tent when he overplayed it. Odine Dunmere: Fellow bearer of the black vine corruption (though Gruvelda severed hers). She has significant knowledge about the pestilence and wants to speak with Odine privately. Investigate the Pestilence: A key lead.

Holt is a registrar at the King's Tourney registration tent. He wears a light blue and gold-trimmed cap and has a well-kept burly mustache. Source: 2026.05.05. He registered Cassian, Aldrich, Azrith, and Odine Dunmere as Cassian's Crushing Crusaders. He charged the 25 gold group entry fee for the Proving Grounds. He placed the party's registration on the "to be watched" shelf. He scheduled the team to report to Tent D on the following in-game day at 6 PM. See Compete in the King's Tourney. On 2026.08.11, greeted the party warmly as "the talk of the fairgrounds," confirmed their promotion from the Proving Grounds to The Menagerie tier, and explained its judging emphasizes spectacle, daring, and mastery rather than simple kills ("any butcher can kill an animal"). Scheduled their bout for the next day at 5 PM in the red tent, opponent bracketed near House Wulfhelm. Also processed House Oswall's unusually large tournament registration this year. On 2026.08.18, confirmed via the public bracket board that the party's Menagerie opponent is Kardis Wulfhelm himself, sponsored under House Wulfhelm. Mentioned unusually heavy mutual scouting/interest between the two camps lately, but stayed coy about further gossip ("I only told them the best things"). Source: 2026.08.18. Was aghast at the party's manticore bout, calling it "the most disrespectful performance" he'd seen in the games, and warned that the game makers, judges, and noble houses would be furious enough to end the party's tournament run—urging them to leave quickly before anyone could react. Source: 2026.09.15.

Ian is an old Oathkeeper knight posted alone at the teleportation circle in Westermere Manor, Havenport. He has a long, unkempt white beard and the look of a man who has been stationed there a long time. Naming note: only Cassian called him "Ian Wren"; the GM never confirmed the surname. Source: 2026.09.22. Took the circle's keystone back from Aldrich when the party arrived. Warned them, "you won't want to linger here long." Recognized Cassian as "Lord Fortescue's son": "people tend to have short memories, don't they... I've been doing this a long time." See House Fortescue. Treated Havenport as Aldrich's home and asked whether he recalled the fall of House Westermere. Wears an amulet that he says keeps the undead away. He tries to find the village children who wander up at night and warn them off the undercroft. A fellow Oathkeeper relieves him every two weeks. Named the blight the Wither and said it is taking more and more of Havenport's weak and sick. His grandfather fought beside King Aldrich against the Dark King. He told the party the veteran Oathkeepers' legend of it (see Investigate the Pestilence), and said the Wither's symptoms resemble what their ancestors suffered. Pointed the party to the Salt House for lodging. Has never met the manor's ghosts. Source: 2026.09.22. Oathkeepers: A long-serving knight of the order. Cassian: Knew of his family. Samantha Westermere: She doesn't know his name.

Jevon traveled with the party to Everdale and guided them into the King's Tourney. He was taken by House Godrin soldiers and interrogated about his magic and his teacher. The party rescued him at the Stone Sanctum graveyard. He is now in hiding and cannot be seen at the fair in daylight. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.05.12. In hiding. After being rescued from the Stone Sanctum graveyard, Jevon slipped into the shadows and is laying low for the coming days. He cannot safely appear at the King's Tourney in daylight because House Godrin will be looking for him. Odine Dunmere holds a communication stone (a custom sending stone, usable once per day): she can send him a short message and receive a reply telepathically. Source: 2026.05.12. On 2026.06.23 he visited the party's tent in person at night, confirmed House Godrin's knights are still actively hunting him by day, and offered to use his cover as an evening armor-and-weapon repairman for tournament knights to gather intelligence or lend magical help. He said he hadn't seen Maralynn in years and believes she "returned to her people in the Vale" (Thornwood Vale). Source: 2026.06.23. At some point in the untranscribed session between 2026.07.14 and 2026.08.11, the party rescued Jevon a second time from House Godrin knights during what the GM called "a bit of a ghost hunt"—no details survive beyond that. Following this, it was learned House Godrin wants Jevon and his sending stone, but more importantly wants to know who gave him the stone—pointing at a third party, plausibly Maralynn. Jevon is now sheltering in the woods near the fairgrounds; the party set up a hidden dead-drop (a hollowed tree stump 50 paces southeast of their tent) to pass him gold and supplies, since he asked for coin to sustain himself while hiding. Azrith, using his new Goggles of Night, read that Jevon "seems scared about something... he's definitely hiding it." Source: 2026.08.11. On 2026.08.25, Cassian reached out to reassure him: House Godrin's real target is Maralynn, not Jevon himself, based on an intercepted letter. Jevon confirmed Maralynn is his teacher and that he hasn't seen her in years—she deliberately keeps away from the mortal realm. He is now weighing whether to search for her himself or simply keep watch, and said he'd stay in contact. Source: 2026.08.25. By 2026.09.15, Jevon had left Everdale for an outpost on the western fringe of the Thornwood Vale, hoping to help distract or mislead the House Godrin scouting party now chasing Odine Dunmere's decoy lead. Odine Dunmere messaged him via her sending stone to let him know the party was heading to Havenport. Source: 2026.09.15. Jevon carries a walking stick and a magical box of ancient elven craftsmanship, identified by Odine as a relic rather than a common trinket. The box glows brightly near Jevon and dims significantly when separated from him; the light flickered erratically while he was in danger at the Stone Sanctum. His teacher is a witch named Maralynn, who found him near death, malnourished and without strength, saw something in him, taught him to survive, gave him the box, and then departed. Jevon encountered her in Everdale but she is from the Thornwood Vale. House Godrin soldiers kidnapped him to interrogate him about his powers and his teacher. One of the two soldiers was already dead when Jevon regained consciousness (apparently killed by the possessing ghost); the other was destroyed by the party. He can conjure images magically, which he offered as a possible alternative to bringing Gruvelda a severed head as proof of the ghost fight. He recommended the Ragged Flagon as a safe place for the party to lodge during the festival. He laughed at Aldrich's joke about the distorted corpse—the first Jevon laugh of the campaign. "Kevin" remains a running joke among the party for his name. Source: 2026.05.12. Odine Dunmere: Rescued him. Holds his communication stone. He trusts her and relies on her for coin/supplies while hiding. Cassian: Returned Jevon's box to him during combat. Jevon shakes his head at Cassian's jokes. Azrith: Finished off the possessed knight that had been draining his captors; later read Jevon's hidden fear via his Goggles of Night. Aldrich: Made Jevon laugh with a joke about the distorted corpse. Maralynn: His teacher and the source of his magical box. She is being hunted by House Godrin—and may be the true target behind House Godrin's interest in Jevon's sending stone. House Godrin: Kidnapped and interrogated him; rescued from their knights a second time in an untranscribed session; he fears their retaliation.

Kardis Wulfhelm is a young noble, likely a prince of House Wulfhelm, seen at Slug's cookhouse during the King's Tourney. He has somewhat pointed ears, very long bright white hair, and wore shiny black armor. Source: 2026.05.05. Aldrich recognized Kardis by reputation and knew him to be reckless. Cassian knew House Wulfhelm won last year's tournament and currently controls the Thornwood Vale. Kardis used an attendant to quietly move nearby patrons so he and his companion could have more space. He watched the party, especially Aldrich, and whispered to his black-armored companion. Confirmed as the party's Menagerie-tier bracket rival, per Holt's bracket board and Rory's reaction (2026.08.18). Also called "Cardus" in dialogue (same pronunciation/character). Prince and heir apparent of House Wulfhelm; per Rory, "one of the best" swordsmen in the house, though not the very best. Cassian privately calls him a "pompous prick." Both camps have reportedly been scouting each other unusually closely ahead of the bout. Source: 2026.08.18. Clarified (2026.08.25): the Menagerie pits contestants against released monsters, not rival champions directly, so the party does not fight Kardis in the ring—his team was bracketed near them and (per an Unseen Servant's scouting) fought a manticore in the match just before the party's own manticore bout. Source: 2026.08.25. House Wulfhelm: Kardis is tied to the ruling family of the house. Aldrich: Aldrich once served a vassal house beneath House Wulfhelm. Compete in the King's Tourney: The party's confirmed Menagerie-bout opponent.

Lady Elwyn Blackwood is Duke Tristan Blackwood's wife, previously glimpsed sitting beside him in the Proving Grounds box but not formally met until she stepped out of the shadows to smooth over Captain Garan's tense warning to the party. She wears a black-and-gold-trimmed gown and carries herself with practiced noble grace. Source: 2026.09.15. Odine Dunmere's Insight check (13) read her as highly intelligent and a social manipulator by nature, in contrast to her husband's more strategist bent—though she came across as genuinely warm and interested in the party. Waved off Garan's tension, framing him as a fiery personality mostly worried about his mercenaries' loyalty. Approved of the party's unconventional Menagerie stunt: "it's nice to see a change of pace around here." Duke Tristan Blackwood: Her husband. Captain Garan: Speaks of him with familiarity, smoothing over his warnings to the party.

Maralynn is a witch from the Thornwood Vale who is spoken of with awe by those who have encountered her. She possesses what Jevon described as "unfathomable power." She found Jevon on the brink of death, malnourished and without strength, recognized something in him, taught him to survive, and then departed. She gave him his magical box before she left. Source: 2026.05.12. Unknown. Jevon has not seen her in years. She is from the Thornwood Vale but was encountered at some point in Everdale. Her current whereabouts are unknown. Source: 2026.05.12. Jevon was instructed to call her "Maralynn" and describes her as a "strange witch." She is from the Thornwood Vale, giving her a connection to the world Odine Dunmere is from and the pestilence Odine is trying to stop. Cassian speculated that Maralynn may be the true prize the noble houses are chasing when they compete over the deed to the Thornwood Vale in the King's Tourney—a hidden reason behind the tournament's political stakes. House Godrin interrogated Jevon specifically about his magic and his teacher, suggesting they are actively searching for her. Per Jevon (2026.06.23), she "returned to her people in the Vale" (Thornwood Vale), the same region where House Godrin works with a dwarven clan to extract mana crystals. Jevon said as early as 2026.05.12 that Godrin "tries so hard to maintain control of the Vale so that they can find her." As of the untranscribed session before 2026.08.11, House Godrin's interest in Jevon's sending stone is now framed as secondary to wanting to know who gave it to him—strongly suggestive that Maralynn, not Jevon, is Godrin's real target. She gave Jevon his magical box, which Odine Dunmere identified as ancient elven craftsmanship—a relic, not a trinket. Source: 2026.05.12. Confirmed alive and located by House Godrin: a letter recovered from White Feather Tor plus Cassian's overheard fragment of Percival Godrin's voice both indicate Godrin no longer believes her to be a dead legend—"they're not chasing a ghost. She's alive. We've already confirmed it." Duke Tristan Blackwood separately knows her only through folklore, as an archmage named Marlin who once served King Aldric the Wise, presumed dead since "the ancient war." To protect her real location, Odine Dunmere fed Blackwood a decoy name and location instead. Source: 2026.08.25. Jevon: Former student. She found him, taught him, gave him his box, and disappeared. Odine Dunmere: Odine wants to find Maralynn because of her connection to the Vale and the pestilence. House Godrin: Actively searching for her; interrogated Jevon to find her location. Thornwood Vale: Maralynn's origin. Investigate the Pestilence: A possible key figure.

Marea Voss is an apothecary at the King's Tourney. She is a dark-skinned, sharp-tongued, witty woman with a silk gown, jewelry, and a mystic herbalist's style. Source: 2026.05.05. She sold four healing potions to Cassian and Odine Dunmere for 38 gold total after Cassian haggled her down. She sold Aldrich a Traveler's Tonic for 8 gold, granting advantage on a future ability check, saving throw, or attack. When Odine mentioned the pestilence in the Thornwood Vale, Marea warned her to seek only true sources and avoid people who exploit misinformation. See Investigate the Pestilence. On 2026.08.11, sold Odine Dunmere two Potions of Greater Healing (150 gp each, haggled to 280 gp total) and negotiated with Cassian (Persuasion 23) to sell a rare Potion of Hill Giant Strength for 280 gp (down from 350 gp). She also keeps rarer stock on hand—a Potion of Growth, and the ingredients for a Potion of Speed (2,000–3,000 gp, declined) and a theoretical Potion of Flight requiring griffon plume or air-elemental essence.

Mauve Marigold is the person Duke Tristan Blackwood sent the party to find in Havenport. They are to stay with her until he sends word. She has not yet been met. Naming note: the GM said "Mauve Mauve Marigold" in the recap, and Ian said "Mav," so the exact spelling is unconfirmed. Source: 2026.09.22. Per Ian, "Mav and her people" have taken refuge in the village from the undead beneath Westermere Manor. She may be among the survivors at the Salt House, but that is unconfirmed. Duke Tristan Blackwood: Directed the party to her. Havenport: Lives there with "her people."

Minnie is a brewer at the King's Tourney and the wife of Slug. Slug called her the best brewer in town. Source: 2026.05.05. She sold Aldrich a bottle of her finest huckleberry mead for one gold. The mead is made locally with huckleberries harvested near the fringes of the Thornwood Vale. Aldrich plans to save the bottle for a victory celebration after the King's Tourney.

Percival Godrin is a member of House Godrin's ruling family, named in Duke Tristan Blackwood's intelligence note on the Godrin camp at White Feather Tor. He frequently moves between the central pavilion, Everdale, and the tourney grounds—making him harder to pin down than family members who stay put. Source: 2026.08.18. Overheard by an invisible, flying Cassian at White Feather Tor's main tent, speaking in hushed tones to an unidentified second party: "Keep your voice down. They're not chasing a ghost. She's alive. We've already confirmed it."—confirming House Godrin has located Maralynn. Source: 2026.08.25. House Godrin: Family member. Golstang Godrin: Presumed relative (patron). White Feather Tor: Frequents the central pavilion here, among other places.

Renny Blackwood is Duke Tristan Blackwood's nephew and manservant. Scrawny, red-faced, and sweaty from carrying his uncle's reward pouch, with white hair and the look of a man in his late 60s. Source: 2026.08.11. Delivered the party's Crown Gauntlet victory reward from Duke Blackwood: roughly 1,500 gold split among the party plus individualized magic items (see Compete in the King's Tourney). Relayed Duke Blackwood's invitation to visit his tent that evening "to discuss business"—not yet acted on by the party. Politely declined Cassian's offer of a drink, citing "other matters to attend," and left the empty reward pouch with the party at Cassian's request before departing. On 2026.08.18, the party set out to find him again after Aldrich was driven to exhaustion level 6 by the King's Cup drinking tournament, hoping he'd know of a cleric who could help before the Menagerie bout—not yet resolved on-page. Granted the party an emergency audience with Duke Blackwood after they told him they had information he was looking for. Left a short good-luck note for the party at Holt's check-in desk ahead of their Menagerie bout: "shorthanded on such short notice... best of luck don't die." Source: 2026.08.25. Rushed into the Ragged Flagon breathless and panicked after the manticore bout to summon the party urgently to Duke Blackwood's tent. Source: 2026.09.15. Duke Tristan Blackwood: His uncle and employer. Cassian: Made light small talk with him; found him a good sport.

Ronan Godrin is a member of House Godrin's ruling family, named in Duke Tristan Blackwood's intelligence note on the Godrin camp at White Feather Tor. He's frequently found around the competitor and training grounds—both the camp's own training grounds and, potentially, the King's Tourney's. Source: 2026.08.18. House Godrin: Family member. Golstang Godrin: Presumed relative (patron). White Feather Tor: Frequents the training grounds there.

Rory is the orc bartender and proprietor of the Ragged Flagon, a makeshift tavern in the King's Tourney campgrounds. He is a practical, no-nonsense host who keeps prices low and expectations lower—his house ale is terrible but effective, and he does not clean up after anyone. Source: 2026.05.19. An orc running a bar is an uncommon sight in this part of the Crownlands. He seems very comfortable and experienced behind the bar. House ale runs 1 silver piece per flagon. Cheap, gut-rumbling, and warm. His only house rule: "Don't get into any fights. I don't like to clean up." He asked Cassian and the party what brought them to the tourney and what bout they were entered in, and seemed genuinely interested. His establishment draws common folk, salt-of-the-earth festival-goers, and tournament participants—not the noble houses. Full name is Rory Greathorn. He won Cassian's 5-gp wager under the double-or-nothing clause (two party members were downed). The payout was already complete by the time the party visited the Coin Master. Source: 2026.06.11. Cassian rolled persuasion 24 to secure the party's multi-day mead supply at half price—12 silver total for several days of Minnie's black currant mead (spiced with cardamom and cinnamon). Source: 2026.06.11. Bet 25 gp against the party completing the Crown Gauntlet once he heard they'd chosen it over straight combat; Cassian took the counter-position. Rory lost—shown in the crowd throwing his hat into the mud in disgust during Cassian's victory speech. Source: 2026.06.23, 2026.07.14. Gave the party free mead "on the house" after losing the bet again, vowing to stop betting against "the Crushing Crusaders." Aldrich used the moment to steal an entire mead barrel from him via Sleight of Hand (19), completely undetected. Source: 2026.08.11. Runs a weekly drinking tournament at the Ragged Flagon, the King's Cup: entry fee in gold, escalating-DC Constitution saves, winner takes the pot plus an oversized brass drinking mug. Was visibly shocked to learn the party's next opponent is House Wulfhelm's own Kardis Wulfhelm, and hedged his future bets accordingly. Took a 5 gp side bet from Cassian backing Aldrich to do well (Cassian won it) and separately facilitated a rigged 20 gp side bet Odine Dunmere arranged against her own success. Refuses to say what's in the tournament's final "King's Mistake" shot. Paid out Aldrich's 90 gp and the mug after Aldrich won the whole tournament, outlasting an unnamed dwarf who died from the final round. Source: 2026.08.18. Revealed he bet against the party in the manticore bout and won handsomely ("you've made me a wealthy man again"), collecting his winnings from the Coin Master before they even arrived. Poured free drinks anyway (two per head, Aldrich's brass mug filled specially) and warned the party to watch their backs—"those nobles, they like to play dirty." Source: 2026.09.15. Ragged Flagon: Rory runs the establishment. Cassian: Introduced himself and the party on the group's first night; Cassian later won a half-price mead deal from him via persuasion, and has now beaten two of his bets against the party. Aldrich: Stole a barrel of his mead undetected.

Samantha Westermere is the ghost of a daughter of House Westermere. She is a floating, silvery woman whose hair drifts in an ethereal wind, haunting the undercroft of her family's home, Westermere Manor. She died in her own room there after "many catastrophes" led to her house's fall. She refuses to pass on until the living restore Havenport to how it was in her childhood. Source: 2026.09.22. She emerged after Azrith leapt into the Curtain: "Bold of your friend to take the gate." She explained that it is "a curtain to the realm of death", and that Azrith may return "if he survives" when it reopens, in a day or a week. She has seen groups go through it together. She showed the party the black veil, which is impenetrable to her. She said she learned "more in the last five minutes than I have in the last five years" from watching them touch it, and believes it is tied to the Curtain. Invited the party to stay in the manor's rooms, but warned that residents of "the other side" might try to possess them. Playful and a little cagey. She blushed at Cassian's flirting, and he promised to return: "A Fortescue always keeps their promise." Doesn't know Ian, the Oathkeeper upstairs. Source: 2026.09.22. House Westermere: Her family. Westermere Manor: Her home and haunt. Cassian: Charmed by him. He promised to come back.

Ser Calder Ross, known as "the Doomfist," is the prized tournament champion of House Wulfhelm. He is a weaponless pugilist who fights with armored gauntlets. House Wulfhelm won last year's King's Tourney largely on his performance. Source: 2026.05.19. Entered in the King's Tourney. Identified by The Masked Figure as one of the two primary obstacles the party will face if they advance far enough in the Proving Grounds bracket. Source: 2026.05.19. Fights without a conventional weapon, using armored gauntlets as his primary offense. Won (or heavily contributed to winning) House Wulfhelm's title at the King's Tourney last year. The Masked Figure implied it could "remove" him as a roadblock for Cassian if Cassian holds up his end of the deal. Reconfirmed on 2026.08.11 as the party's Menagerie-tier bout was scheduled near a House Wulfhelm-bracketed opponent: Ross himself is well above this bracket's weight class and will not be faced directly at this stage. House Wulfhelm: Their prized champion and primary tournament asset.

Sir Thorin Cassavar, known at the tournaments as "the Crow," is House Godrin's fiercest warrior and tournament champion. He stands nearly 9–10 feet tall, clad in arcane relic armor and helm and wielding an enchanted axe—all gifted to him by the house. Some say the armor itself enlarges his frame. Cassian spotted him for the first time while eavesdropping invisibly at White Feather Tor and deliberately avoided drawing his attention. Source: 2026.08.25. Recognized on sight by Cassian from prior tournament championship matches he's watched. His armor, helm, and axe are all arcane relics supplied by House Godrin. House Godrin: Their champion and fiercest warrior. White Feather Tor: Seen among the guards patrolling the Godrin family camp.

Slug is the large, rotund owner of a cookhouse at the King's Tourney. He is known for smoked pork and remembered Cassian from a previous tourney visit. Source: 2026.05.05. Slug is about six and a half feet tall and wears off-white commoner's clothes and an off-white apron. He serves smoked pork, mead, and food gathered from nearby vendors. He is married to Minnie. He accommodated Odine Dunmere with cheese, crackers, and mushrooms after she reacted badly to the meat.

A manticore forced to fight in The Menagerie, freed by Cassian during what was meant to be a routine tournament bout. Bound to its captors by a trebuchet rigged with a steel net—positioned to recapture anything that tried to flee the arena—it initially fought the party, but broke off once Cassian offered genuine freedom instead of combat. Cassian flew it to the trebuchet, charmed the operator into standing down, and let it destroy the machine. It departed unnamed, promising to visit the party's camp for meat and ale, and to find a name of its own. Source: 2026.09.08. Speaks Common, and is clearly bound or trained rather than a mindless beast. Deeply afraid of "its masters," who it said would kill it regardless of the bout's outcome. Scarred from prior mistreatment, visible even before the fight began. Left unnamed; asked Cassian to help name it, but Cassian deferred: "a man such as myself should not decide the name of such an incredible beast." Cassian: Freed it from its captors and the arena; invited to visit the party's camp. The Menagerie: Its former place of captivity and forced combat.

An unnamed figure that appears to Cassian in his dreams. It wears a trimmed gown and regalia and a mask that conceals nearly its entire face, revealing only mischievous eyes. It speaks with intelligence, amusement, and a preference for long-term loyalties over coin. It gifted Cassian his magical dice in a prior dream—the same dice that trails a burgundy light when rolled. Source: 2026.05.19. Active. A deal was struck with Cassian during the long rest before the first Proving Grounds bout. The figure's identity and true nature are unknown. Source: 2026.05.19. Cassian's obligations: Continue stirring trouble among the noble houses. Keep the party together through the tournament. Keep Odine Dunmere close: "I find her interesting and relevant; don't let her out of your sight." The Masked Figure's obligations: Pull strings to remove "immovable roadblocks" in the tournament—named as Ser Calder Ross (House Wulfhelm's champion) and House Godrin's champion. Find the answer to how Cassian's family acquired the dice and deliver it before the final bout. Source: 2026.05.19. The figure called Cassian "clever boy" and said: "I don't like to trade in gloria coin. I prefer loyalties—skills ones that cannot be bought." It framed the arrangement as a "partnership" rather than an employer/employee relationship.
