It expressed interest in both Cassian's party and specifically in Odine; it found the presence of two tieflings together "interesting." It does not know how Cassian's family acquired the dice—this is a genuine mystery to it as well. Dream appearances take place in mundane locations (the Ragged Flagon); whether this is Cassian's subconscious or a true visitation is unknown. Cassian: The primary contact. It gifted him his dice and has appeared in at least two separate dreams. Odine Dunmere: The figure considers her "interesting and relevant" for unknown reasons.

Valerie Godrin is a member of House Godrin's ruling family, named in Duke Tristan Blackwood's intelligence note on the Godrin camp at White Feather Tor. She regularly leaves camp, making her the most accessible Godrin family member away from the family—a notable lead for the party's planned investigation. Source: 2026.08.18. House Godrin: Family member. Golstang Godrin: Presumed relative (patron). Investigate House Godrin: Flagged as the easiest family member to approach outside camp.

Virellan Le'Strange is a flamboyant bard or observer at the King's Tourney. He wears a mask over one eye, royal purple robes, a soft cap with a fiery plume, and carries a drum at his sash. Source: 2026.05.05. He greeted the party shortly after they entered the fair. He introduced Aldrich to Minnie when Aldrich asked where to find good ale. He seems more interested in observing stories than performing them. Reappeared at the King's Tourney during session 2026.06.11. He addressed Cassian as "Lord Fortescue," confirming Cassian's family house name as House Fortescue. Source: 2026.06.11.

House Blackwood is a lower-tier vassal house at the King's Tourney. They hold a smaller parcel of land loaned to them by one of the greater houses and are not one of the big three noble houses. They do not typically win tournaments. Their representative at the current tournament is Duke Tristan Blackwood. Source: 2026.06.02. Duke Tristan Blackwood watched the party's first Proving Grounds bout from the noble box and made eye contact with Cassian afterward, signaling interest. On a similar level of nobility to Cassian's family vassal house under House Wulfhelm. House Blackwood is a vassal of House Corwyn, one of the three dominant houses at the tournament. Duke Blackwood operates within Corwyn's sphere of influence and reports up to them. Source: 2026.06.11. Duke Blackwood formalized a sponsorship deal with the party at 8% of prize money, providing a 750 gp advance and four combat items. Source: 2026.06.11. Duke Tristan Blackwood: Their midlord representative at the King's Tourney. House Corwyn: Their liege house; House Blackwood is a vassal of Corwyn. King's Tourney: Competing house with modest standing; now sponsors Cassian's Crushing Crusaders.

House Corwyn is one of the three dominant noble houses at the King's Tourney and in the broader Crownlands. The GM's stated faction theme: Truth Seekers—their interest in power runs through information, scholarship, and the arcane arts rather than pure military might or wealth. Their retainers are identified by silver armor. Source: 2026.06.11, GM faction notes. One of the "big three" alongside House Godrin (Mage Power) and House Wulfhelm (Militant Peace). House Blackwood and Duke Tristan Blackwood are vassals of House Corwyn, which places them directly in Corwyn's sphere of influence at the tournament. Their champion and broader tournament strategy are not yet known to the party. Their true motive, per Blackwood: House Corwyn believes the Thornwood Vale conceals a secret that could unite the lesser noble houses to rise up against Godrin and Wulfhelm. They've sought this secret for nearly a century but cannot act on it without holding the Vale's title outright—which Wulfhelm currently holds. Per Blackwood, Corwyn's self-image is that they're clever enough to understand everyone else's game. Source: 2026.08.18. Duke Tristan Blackwood, their vassal, is a wildcard rather than a loyal company man: he says he'd relish seeing all three great houses (including his own liege, Corwyn) lose the tournament this year—something unprecedented in its hundred-year history. Source: 2026.08.18. House Blackwood: Their vassal; Duke Tristan Blackwood reports up to House Corwyn. House Godrin: Fellow big-three house; rivals. House Wulfhelm: Fellow big-three house; rivals. King's Tourney: A major competitor for the Thornwood Vale deed.

House Fortescue is Cassian's family house, of celestial or semi-divine bloodline—descended from a lineage cut off from the divine but still carrying celestial heritage. Confirmed as a vassal of House Wulfhelm for roughly 60 years (established 40 years after King Aldrich's reign ended, around a century ago). Source: 2026.06.11, 2026.08.18. Duke Tristan Blackwood, despite "running in a lot of circles," has never once heard House Wulfhelm acknowledge or claim House Fortescue as a vassal—and finds this odd enough to remark on directly. Source: 2026.08.18. Cassian deflected the question rather than explain: "There are few who remember us fondly... that is part of the reason I am here." This implies some falling-out, disgrace, or forgotten history attached to the house that Cassian has not yet revealed to the party or the wiki. Source: 2026.08.18. Cassian's family signet ring (a falling star meeting its own tail, ouroboros-like) marks the house as old-blooded nobility. See Cassian. Blackwood did not consider the Fortescue name "risky" to associate with, despite the discrepancy. The old Oathkeeper Ian in Havenport recognized the name at once and called Cassian "Lord Fortescue's son": "people tend to have short memories, don't they." Source: 2026.09.22. Cassian: Scion of the house. House Wulfhelm: Nominal liege house—though Wulfhelm apparently does not acknowledge the vassalage publicly. Duke Tristan Blackwood: Suspicious of the unacknowledged vassalage; pressed Cassian on it directly.

House Godrin is one of the three most powerful noble houses in the Crownlands. The GM's stated faction theme: Mage Power—known for mana crystals, artifacts, and magical wealth. Its current patron is Golstang Godrin. The other two dominant houses are House Wulfhelm (Militant Peace) and House Corwyn (Truth Seekers). Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.06.11, GM faction notes. Their knights or retainers at the King's Tourney wore matte white armor and displayed a white banner. Cassian recognized them and avoided drawing their attention. They believe in the right to rule and are one of the major houses that frequently win the King's Tourney. Cassian knows they have a ruthless drive that common folk may not fully see. Two of their foot soldiers abducted Jevon from the King's Tourney and interrogated him in the Stone Sanctum graveyard about his magic and his teacher, a witch named Maralynn. Both soldiers are now dead—one killed by the possessing ghost, the other destroyed by the party in combat. Source: 2026.05.12. Cassian speculated that House Godrin's real interest in controlling the Thornwood Vale is to locate Maralynn, who is from the Vale and wields extraordinary power. Source: 2026.05.12. Their tournament dominance is explained mechanically: they compete every year specifically to harvest mana crystals, working closely with a dwarven clan in the Vale—the arcane fuel source powering their armada of weapons, armor, and artifacts and reinforcing their claim to the throne. The tourney's grand prize (King's Cup + a deed to the Vale) is why they and House Wulfhelm fight hardest for it every year. Source: 2026.06.23. In an untranscribed session before 2026.08.11, House Godrin knights attacked the party again in a bid to recapture Jevon; the party drove them off. It was learned Godrin wants Jevon's sending stone but, more importantly, wants to know who gave it to him—implying their real target is a third party, plausibly Maralynn. Naming note: for much of session 2026.08.11 the party mistakenly referred to this house as "House Oswall" before the GM corrected it mid-session. House Godrin is the white-armored house pursuing Jevon; House Oswall is the unrelated, unarmored religious house. All wiki pages use the corrected names. Armor color note: on 2026.08.18, the table corrected a running mix-up at the table: House Godrin wears white armor and House Wulfhelm wears black—confirmed as the GM's actual intent. Several earlier session logs had described Jevon's Godrin abductors as "black-armored" in error; these have been corrected to white to match. Keeps meticulous ledgers of their activity at an outpost on the outskirts of the King's Fair, per Gruvelda Duskbelt—an unconfirmed but concrete lead for learning why they want Jevon. Source: 2026.08.11. Reportedly a paying client of Gruvelda Duskbelt's smithy (black plate armor commissions observed); she neither confirms nor denies this, framing herself as a neutral mercenary. Source: 2026.08.11. Duke Tristan Blackwood describes them as unusually active lately—"asking a lot of questions," "sticking their noses in shady corners"—and reports rumors they've been kidnapping children. As a young competitor himself, Blackwood personally once witnessed House Godrin abducting hedge mages, and wonders what "frightened one of the most powerful arcane families in the Crownlands badly enough to resort to kidnapping." Source: 2026.08.18. Per Blackwood, Godrin's self-image: they believe this year's King's Tourney already belongs to them. Alongside House Wulfhelm, they have traded control of the Thornwood Vale between them for nearly a decade via the tournament. Source: 2026.08.18. Blackwood gave the party a written intelligence note listing names and locations tied to Godrin's camp activity, pointing to the Messenger Tent at White Feather Tor—not yet investigated. Source: 2026.08.18. The Godrin family camp is White Feather Tor, in the Eastern Tourney Grounds: 30 people total, 6–8 knights in matte-white armor, 12–15 men-at-arms in white-and-grey livery, plus servants, messengers, grooms, and arcane attendants. Security tightens considerably after dark along the perimeter. Named family members (per Blackwood's note): Golstang Godrin (patron, central pavilion, heavily guarded), Percival Godrin (moves between the pavilion, Everdale, and the tourney grounds), Emberlee Godrin (stays in camp, rarely alone), Valerie Godrin (regularly leaves camp—the most accessible family member outside it), Ronan Godrin (frequently at the training grounds). Champion identified: Sir Thorin Cassavar, "the Crow"—a nearly 9–10-foot-tall warrior in arcane relic armor and helm, wielding an enchanted axe, spotted patrolling White Feather Tor. Source: 2026.08.25. On 2026.08.25, the party infiltrated White Feather Tor and confirmed via an intercepted letter and overheard conversation (Percival Godrin's voice) that House Godrin has located Maralynn and knows she is alive, not the dead legend they'd assumed. The party fed Duke Tristan Blackwood a decoy lead to protect her real location. Spell draught: an Oathkeeper acolyte at the Gleaming Keep said the teleportation circles run on spell draught, a liquid transmuted from the mana crystals mined in the Thornwood Vale that Godrin harvests whenever it holds the deed. House Godrin was "influential in the discovery" of spell draught, which took nearly 60 years to work out. Source: 2026.09.22.

House Oswall is a nomadic religious group that arrives at the King's Tourney each year to claim legitimacy to the Crownlands throne. The GM's stated faction theme: Illegitimate. They have never been formally deeded land by King Aldrich and are considered an illegitimate house by the established nobility. They are generally regarded as a joke among the noble houses and are typically humiliated at the tournament before departing. Source: 2026.06.11, GM faction notes. Identified by green, gold, and purple robes; priests, nuns, floats, banners, and trumpets accompany their arrival parade. Common folk show genuine interest in their procession; established nobles are dismissive. Aldrich recalled their history with an investigation roll of 12: never deeded land, claims throne legitimacy, comes every year, typically humiliated. Cassian confirmed from noble knowledge: they are considered a standing joke among legitimate houses. Their religious nature and nomadic lifestyle suggest a distinct theological or prophetic basis for their throne claim, though details are not yet established. Naming note: for much of session 2026.08.11 the party mistakenly used "House Oswall" to refer to the white-armored knights pursuing Jevon—that house is actually House Godrin. House Oswall itself is unarmored, unrelated to the Jevon plot, and had no combat presence in that confusion. Fielded three unarmored dignitaries registering for The Menagerie tournament tier on 2026.08.11—an unusually large showing, more entries than any prior year, though still treated as underdogs/a laughing stock by onlookers given their lack of military background. King's Tourney: Attend annually to press their claim; never win. Aldrich: Has passing historical knowledge of the group. Cassian: Offered their registering dignitaries a backhanded blessing—"nothing legitimizes a house faster than surviving in front of witnesses."

House Troth is a minor, lesser-known vassal house of House Wulfhelm. Aldrich once served under them—not as nobility, but in a rank-and-file guard/security capacity—before leaving "the seaside" to see the world at an old friend's encouragement. Source: 2026.08.18. Confirmed live at the table as Aldrich's former house (chosen between two options offered—House Troth and House Hawk). This is the same house previously tracked in the wiki only as an unnamed House Wulfhelm vassal—this session finally gave it a name. Duke Tristan Blackwood advised Aldrich to keep the connection quiet; Aldrich is confident no one at the tournament would recognize him from it. House Wulfhelm: Liege house. Aldrich: Former low-ranking guard.

House Westermere is a fallen noble house of Havenport. Its cliffside home, Westermere Manor, now stands ruined above the town. "Many catastrophes" led to the house's fall, and Havenport has been in disarray ever since. The manor looks 10–15 years abandoned. Source: 2026.09.22. Aldrich has "heard of their fall" but avoids Havenport's history. He left town roughly eight or nine years ago. The only known member is the ghost Samantha Westermere, who died in the manor's undercroft. Its liege house and the details of its fall are unknown. Source: 2026.09.22. Westermere Manor: Their ancestral home. Samantha Westermere: A daughter of the house, now a ghost. Havenport: The town they once ruled or presided over (inferred).

House Wulfhelm is one of the three most powerful noble houses in the Crownlands. The GM's stated faction theme: Militant Peace—military dominance framed as the guarantor of order rather than raw conquest. They won last year's King's Tourney and currently hold the title and deed to the Thornwood Vale. The other two dominant houses are House Godrin (Mage Power) and House Corwyn (Truth Seekers). Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.06.11, GM faction notes. The house descends from Beowyn, who was deeded lands by King Aldrich centuries ago. A very old Beowyn, fourth of his line, remains the great-grandfather of the household. His son Eodwin is the current salt-and-pepper knightly lord who rules the house, and Kardis Wulfhelm is likely Eodwin's son. Source: 2026.05.05. Aldrich once worked as a soldier or security for a vassal house beneath House Wulfhelm. Cassian's family house is a vassal of House Wulfhelm; this gave him enough credibility to negotiate lodging in the house's noble camp section (Boarhead Tor) for one night. Source: 2026.05.19. Their prized tournament champion is Ser Calder Ross, a weaponless pugilist who fights with armored gauntlets. He won last year's tournament for the house. The Masked Figure identified him as one of the major obstacles the party will face. Source: 2026.05.19. Kardis Wulfhelm had a full bedchamber tent reserved at Boarhead Tor for his return party the night before the party's first bout. Source: 2026.05.19. Currently holds the title/deed to the Thornwood Vale from last year's win. Confirmed black armor (in contrast to House Godrin's white). Has traded control of the Vale back and forth with House Godrin for nearly a decade via the tournament. Per Blackwood, Wulfhelm's self-image is that their strength and status entitle them to win. Source: 2026.08.18. The party's Menagerie-tier bout is confirmed against Kardis Wulfhelm himself—prince and heir of the house, one of its best swordsmen—not Ser Calder Ross, who remains above this bracket. Source: 2026.08.18. House Fortescue (Cassian's family) and House Troth (Aldrich's former house) are both vassals of House Wulfhelm. Notably, Duke Tristan Blackwood—despite knowing many circles—has never once heard Wulfhelm publicly acknowledge House Fortescue as a vassal, an unresolved thread. Source: 2026.08.18.

The Oathkeepers are three orders of knights bound under one oath in Everdale. They guard the Gleaming Keep, protect the Empty Throne, police the King's Tourney, and help oversee the city's economy and settlement. Source: 2026.05.05. The Oathkeepers are composed of three distinct knightly orders, each with its own banner, that agreed to a shared code and merged their purpose after King Aldrich's reign ended. They are the only three orders that still survive from that era. Source: 2026.05.12. | Banner | Emblem | Notes | |---|---|---| | Green shield | A stag / antlers | The same order as Sir Televast, the knight the party encountered before reaching Everdale | | Red shield | An ember flame | — | | Silver crest | A helm with two crossed swords | — | The orders patrol Everdale's hamlet streets in pairs and wear their own emblems. Cassian recognized all three as the oldest surviving knightly orders in the current era of men. Source: 2026.05.12. The Oathkeepers preserve the keep and throne because they believe King Aldrich will someday return to rule again. They tell children this as a bedtime story—that the king will emerge from the stone and unite all the realms. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.05.12. In an untranscribed session before 2026.08.11, the party learned that one of the Oathkeeper knights they met on the road into Everdale is privately fed up with the order's oath-bound inability to act against a new blight called the Wither—the same phenomenon the party has been calling "the hollowing." This is the first time the blight has been given a proper name in play. See Investigate the Pestilence. Source: 2026.08.11. The Oathkeepers maintain a few teleportation circles that survive from King Aldrich's time, including one in the Gleaming Keep and one in Westermere Manor, Havenport. Using a circle requires their permission and a tribute; Duke Tristan Blackwood paid roughly 5,000 gp. A robed acolyte traces the circle with spell draught, a liquid transmuted from Thornwood Vale mana crystals, and the traveler speaks the destination while holding a metal keystone. A lone knight, Ian, guards the Havenport circle and is relieved every two weeks. Source: 2026.09.22. Veteran Oathkeepers "believe the old stories" of the Dark King (also called the Nightmare King), a corrupting ruler from a far realm whom King Aldrich defeated alone, leaving only a statue of himself in the Vale. Ian's grandfather fought in that war. See Investigate the Pestilence. Source: 2026.09.22.

Active. Cassian, Aldrich, Azrith, and Odine Dunmere competed as Cassian's Crushing Crusaders, won their first Proving Grounds bout, and then completed the Crown Gauntlet obstacle-course bout (started 2026.06.23, finished 2026.07.14)—the first team to clear it in over seven years, per the tourney's own bookkeeper. The party has now advanced past the Proving Grounds into The Menagerie, a gladiatorial beast-arena tier judged on spectacle, daring, and mastery. Their Menagerie bracket slot, scheduled 5 PM red tent, was bracketed near Kardis Wulfhelm himself (prince and heir of House Wulfhelm)—but the Menagerie pits contestants against released monsters rather than rival champions directly, and the party's actual opponent was a manticore, freed rather than killed (see below). Aldrich was driven to exhaustion level 6 after the King's Cup drinking tournament on 2026.08.18, putting the bout at serious risk, but was treated down to exhaustion level 1 by 2026.08.25 (see Cure Aldrich's Exhaustion, resolved). Sponsored by Duke Tristan Blackwood (House Blackwood) at 8% of prize money; 750 gp advance, four combat items, and a 1,500 gp Gauntlet victory reward (with more magic items) already delivered. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.06.02, 2026.06.11, 2026.07.14, 2026.08.11, 2026.08.18, 2026.08.25. A 40-foot obstacle tower rising from a mud pit: sloped mud stairs → spinning balance logs → a guarded wall platform → rotating gear-driven platforms → a final guarded platform and bell, which all four party members must reach and ring together. Scored on Cheer Marks (crowd-pleasing successes) and Mud Marks (embarrassing failures)—10 of either triggers a team-wide boon or bane; no lethal force allowed against the four obstacle guards. The party finished with Cheer Marks maxed at 10/10 (a permanent +1d4 to Gauntlet rolls, stacking with Bless) and low Mud Marks, ringing the bell with six seconds left on the clock. Duke Tristan Blackwood watched the win with only a reserved slow clap. Source: 2026.06.23, 2026.07.14. A gladiatorial "fantasy bullfighting" arena tier above the Proving Grounds: captured monsters are released into the ring for champions to fight in front of thousands of spectators. Past creatures advertised on posters include a steel-plated gorgon-bull, a medusa-type monster, and a griffon. Judged on spectacle, daring, and mastery, not just kills, per Holt. Source: 2026.08.11. Cassian paid the 25 gold group entry fee. Holt entered the team on the "to be watched" shelf. The Proving Grounds can attract scouts and sponsors; a strong showing could lead toward the Grand Stage. The Proving Grounds is a multi-phase spectacle: Phase 1: Puzzle-like challenges testing ingenuity and teamwork under pressure. Phase 2: Dangerous beast encounters (bears have been observed; no owlbears). The arena is muddy, packed with sawdust and blood, with cheap banners overhead and active betting rings running alongside. Strong parties get approached by scouts and sponsors immediately after their bout. Weak parties limp out or leave on stretchers. Source: 2026.05.19. Cassian's first bet: Lost. The 5-gp wager was already paid out to Rory Greathorn (Rory) under the double-or-nothing clause—two party members went unconscious. No appeal was accepted by the Coin Master. Source: 2026.05.19, 2026.06.02, 2026.06.11. Crown Gauntlet wager: The party pooled 50 gp on themselves at 3× underdog odds (bookkeeper Ulkaf); Rory bet 25 gp against them, and Cassian took the counter-position. The party won both—150 gp paid into party funds. Source: 2026.06.23, 2026.08.11. Aldrich's Sentinel Shield: Received from Gruvelda Duskbelt as reward for the ghost job. Advantage on initiative and perception; requires an action to swap modes. Source: 2026.05.19. The Masked Figure has offered to clear Ser Calder Ross (House Wulfhelm) and House Godrin's champion from Cassian's path — if the party holds up their end of the deal. Source: 2026.05.19. Duke Tristan Blackwood (House Blackwood) noticed the party's performance and is expected to approach as a potential sponsor. Source: 2026.06.02. Crown Gauntlet victory reward (delivered by Renny Blackwood, 2026.08.11): 1,500 gp (400 gp each) plus individual magic items—Aldrich a +1 Greatsword, Azrith Goggles of Night, Odine Dunmere a Shadowfell Shard, Cassian the Eyes of Charming. Duke Blackwood has also invited the party to his tent "to discuss business"—not yet fulfilled. Promised intel: Duke Tristan Blackwood agreed to dig up intelligence on House Godrin's weaknesses through his House Corwyn contacts, contingent on a strong Gauntlet showing—now due. See also Investigate House Godrin. Rory's weekly drinking tournament: escalating-DC Constitution saves against a large field of contestants, with exhaustion accumulating on failures. Aldrich won the whole thing on 2026.08.18, outlasting an unnamed dwarf who died on the tournament's final round ("King's Mistake"). Active. Odine Dunmere came to Everdale hoping to find advice or aid for the pestilence ravaging the Thornwood Vale. The blight is now named the Wither and is confirmed to be spreading into the Crownlands. Gruvelda Duskbelt has revealed that Odine's grandmother Mara sacrificed herself to hold it back, and that the King's famed "victory" over it about 150 years ago was a lie. Source: 2026.05.05, 2026.05.12, 2026.06.11, 2026.08.18. The pestilence affects plants, animals, and people in the Thornwood Vale. The pestilence is related to the mist entity and appears to be a manifestation of its malignant energy or magic. The corrupted horse seen before the party reached Everdale resembled what Odine has witnessed at home, suggesting the entity's curse is affecting things outside the Vale. Odine has black tentacle-like lines or scarring on her arm similar to the corruption. She told Jevon she has carried them for "about 15 years" (since roughly age 10–11). Source: 2026.05.12. Marea Voss warned Odine that many people exploit misinformation about the pestilence and told her to seek true sources. Source: 2026.05.05. Gruvelda Duskbelt survived the same corruption by severing her own hand. She keeps the preserved hand in a wooden box and wears a prosthetic. She said plainly: "None of these people know what's coming." Source: 2026.05.12. Maralynn, the witch who taught Jevon, is from the Thornwood Vale and wields power that Jevon described as "unfathomable." House Godrin is actively trying to find her, possibly for her knowledge of the Vale or the entity. Source: 2026.05.12. Once Odine Dunmere showed her the 100-year-old straw doll from the Vale, Gruvelda Duskbelt opened up about the blight: She personally knew Mara, Odine's grandmother. They became "long friends" after meeting by the river when Gruvelda was young. Mara "sacrificed herself—a sacrifice no longer remembered by most of these humans." Odine confirmed that Mara died at 71 and that the entity is as powerful now as when Mara first cast it back. Gruvelda recognized Odine as one of the Touched: "Mara told me about your lineage and the burden you have borne." The lifespans of the Touched have been dwindling over the generations, and she feared none might remain. She confirmed that the hollowing (the blight) is spreading faster than ever and has begun appearing in the Crown Lands. Mortals still believe the King defeated the hollowing about 150 years ago. Odine, tearful, called it "Lies." Gruvelda's closing counsel: "True power comes from within." The conversation set the party's purpose: win the King's Tourney so that the Vale's deed stays out of the great houses' hands. Source: 2026.06.11. Gruvelda Duskbelt: She has first-hand experience with the curse and agreed to speak with Odine in depth after the first festival week. — done (2026.06.11); see above. She remains a key ally and knows more about Mara's line. Maralynn: A witch from the Thornwood Vale who may know the entity or the nature of the pestilence. Her current location is unknown; Jevon is her last known connection. Marea Voss: Warned against misinformation. Could be revisited if more evidence or symptoms appear. Determine whether House Godrin's drive to control the Thornwood Vale is connected to finding Maralynn, exploiting the pestilence, or something else entirely. Determine whether House Wulfhelm's current control of the Vale connects to the spread or concealment of the pestilence. In an untranscribed session before 2026.08.11, the blight was given a proper name for the first time: the Wither. The names the pestilence, the hollowing, the blight and the Wither all refer to the same corruption. An Oathkeeper knight the party met on the road into Everdale is privately fed up with the order's oath-bound inability to act against it. See Oathkeepers. Source: 2026.08.11. Confirmed spreading to the Crownlands: Duke Tristan Blackwood confirmed directly to Odine Dunmere that the blight has begun affecting the Crownlands themselves, not just the Thornwood Vale—supplying the word "blight" himself before she could finish describing it. Source: 2026.08.18. In Havenport, the old Oathkeeper Ian told the legend the veteran Oathkeepers believe: The Dark King (also called the Nightmare King) was a ruler from a "far realm," not of men, elves or dwarves, and "the very essence of corruption itself." It began with fairies and will-o'-wisps luring children to their doom, then learned to corrupt people from within and make them part of its mind. King Aldrich marched against it with all his forces and nearly lost. Ian's grandfather fought at his side. Aldrich then withdrew his army and went on alone with only his elite circle of mages. The Dark King was defeated, and "all that was found left of him in the Vale was a statue of himself." No one knows what King Aldrich did that day. Why it matters: Ian says the Wither's symptoms resemble what their ancestors suffered in that war. The Wither is now taking victims in Havenport too. Odine Dunmere has seen the statue with her own eyes: King Aldrich kneeling with his sword in the ground, alone in the Vale's forest. She said the tale is "very similar" to her family's stories of the entity and of those who fought it. The legend is widespread folklore among men; Aldrich and Cassian both grew up hearing versions of it. This bears on the "King's victory 150 years ago" that Gruvelda and Odine call a lie. Whether the Dark King and the Vale's entity are the same being is unconfirmed. Source: 2026.09.22. Books or records about the Dark King war may exist "amongst the wealthy, those that keep libraries." Havenport has little literature. The convergence of the ethereal and material planes in the Westermere Manor undercroft may be connected to the rise in deaths. This is unconfirmed.

The arcane House Godrin has been hunting the young mage Jevon to reach his teacher, Maralynn, a legendary witch of the Vale they have now confirmed is alive. It is her first sign that the curse has escaped her homeland. See 2026.05.05. 2026.05.05 "The King's Fair" The party reaches Everdale, with the Gleaming Keep shining above a sprawling festival. Cassian glimpses the black, tentacle-like marks on Odine's arm. The party registers for the Proving Grounds and meets the tourney's colorful locals: the registrar Holt, the cook Slug, the brewer Minnie, the apothecary Marea Voss and the bard Virellan Le'Strange. They also catch sight of Kardis Wulfhelm, prince of the house that holds the Vale's deed. Then Jevon vanishes, taken by white-armored knights, and Azrith finds his box dropped in the mud. 2026.05.12 "The Stone Sanctum" The party pitches itself as "ghost hunters" to the dwarven smith Gruvelda Duskbelt. She shows Odine a severed hand bearing the same corruption; she cut off her own to survive it. Following rumors of nobles meddling in a hilltop graveyard, the party finds Jevon bound at the Stone Sanctum and destroys the ghost-possessed House Godrin soldier guarding him. Jevon reveals that Godrin wanted his teacher, a witch of the Vale named Maralynn. He goes into hiding and gives Odine a sending stone. 2026.05.19 "A Deal in Dreams" At the commoners' tavern, the Ragged Flagon, run by the orc Rory, the party convinces Gruvelda that the ghost job is done. She arms Aldrich with a Sentinel Shield and points them to her brother, Grimhall Duskbelt. Cassian talks the party into a borrowed tent on the noble hill of Boarhead Tor. That night, The Masked Figure visits his dreams and strikes a bargain: keep Odine close and stir trouble among the houses, and the Figure will clear the tourney's champions from his path and reveal where his family's strange dice came from. 2026.06.02 "First Blood in the Mud" In their first bout, Cassian and Azrith are both knocked out. Aldrich holds the line alone until Odine revives them, and the Crusaders win to a roaring crowd. The minor lord Duke Tristan Blackwood takes notice. Cassian's side bet is lost on a technicality. 2026.06.11 "The Straw Doll" Blackwood sponsors the party for 8% of any winnings, paying a 750 gp advance and magic items collected at Clover Hill. Cassian is publicly named "Lord Fortescue," heir of House Fortescue. Odine finds a century-old straw doll from the Vale, which unlocks Gruvelda's trust. The smith reveals that she knew Odine's grandmother Mara, who sacrificed herself to cast the entity back. She names Odine one of the Touched. And she confirms that the King's "victory" over the blight 150 years ago was a lie. Gruvelda gifts Odine an Elven Chain and Cassian the mysterious Chain of the Unbroken. 2026.06.23 "The Crown Gauntlet, Part One" Jevon slips into camp at night; he is still hunted. Cassian learns that House Godrin wins the tourney to mine mana crystals in the Vale. The party bets 50 gp on themselves at 3× odds, hypes the crowd, and begins the Crown Gauntlet, a 40-foot obstacle tower over a mud pit. Illusions and laughter spells neutralize most of the guards before the clock is paused. 2026.07.14 "Six Seconds Left" The party maxes out the crowd's cheers, scales the wall, frees a jammed gear-tower with Cassian's chain, and hauls Odine up in a last-second rescue. All four ring the bell with six seconds to spare, the first team to finish in seven years. Blackwood offers only a slow, reserved clap. The party buys its own campsite, learns the blight's true name, the Wither, from a disillusioned Oathkeeper, and rescues Jevon from Godrin's knights a second time. The Freed Manticore flies off promising to visit. The paying crowd boos and the judges are in uproar, while peasants on the cliffs cheer. Blackwood slips out of his box without a word. 2026.09.15 "That Was Genius" The party flees in a haze of burning banners. The lone Oathkeeper Ian tells them the legend of the Dark King, a corrupting power from a far realm.
